A progressive ablation study compares Pix2Pix, NSNet-Base, NSNet-D, and TransNSNet. Image-level performance was summarized over a fixed convergence window (epochs 80-101) from one training run per model. TransNSNet achieved the best mean value in nine of ten metrics, whereas NSNet-Base achieved the highest visual saliency-induced index. For fixed-fraction high-intensity regions, NSNet-D was marginally higher in slice-level recall and balanced accuracy, but the equal-weight patient-level values were nearly identical and the highest Dice values shifted to TransNSNet. These differences were small relative to between-patient variability. In the separate adaptive patient-level analysis (n=10), no pairwise model difference remained statistically significant after Holm correction. TransNSNet also had a substantially smaller parameter footprint than the original next-scale models. These findings indicate promising image-quality trends, but they do not establish statistical superiority or clinical validity; synthesized PET-like images should not be interpreted as substitutes for clinically acquired PET.

items.title_en: CatchUp: Depth-Aware Re-Admission of Visual Tokens for Efficient Large Vision-Language Models
items.abstract_en: Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs) repeatedly process hundreds of visual tokens across decoder layers, incurring substantial computation and memory costs. Existing inference-time visual token pruning methods often irreversibly remove low-ranked tokens, although the set of visual tokens receiving high query-conditioned attention can change across decoder depth. Recoverable routing preserves skipped tokens for later reconsideration, but re-admits them with stale representations after bypassing intermediate transformations. We further find that replacing stale re-admitted states with their current-depth oracle states from a full-token reference trajectory substantially improves grounding performance. We therefore propose CatchUp, a training-free framework for depth-aware visual-token re-admission. CatchUp repeatedly re-evaluates query-conditioned visual relevance, processes only selected visual tokens through each decoder interval, and preserves deferred tokens for later re-admission. Upon re-admission, CatchUp approximates missed representation evolution using reference-to-current transition signals from semantically and spatially related visual tokens. Across three referring-expression grounding datasets and six multimodal benchmarks, CatchUp achieves the highest average relative retention in both benchmark groups at 64-, 128-, and 192-token budgets. At a 64-token budget with 88.9% fewer active visual tokens, CatchUp retains 92.17% of the full model's performance on average across six multimodal benchmarks while reducing end-to-end latency by 8.0%. Code is available at https://github.com/pej0918/CatchUp

items.title_en: Look, Reason, Draw a Region: Recursive Refinement for Spatial Context Prediction
items.abstract_en: Spatial context prediction requires visual grounding and spatial reasoning to identify vacant regions relative to objects in a scene. Spatial relationships and physical constraints remain challenging for large vision-language models (VLMs). Recursive reasoning has demonstrated strong performance on discrete and abstract reasoning tasks, motivating its use for improving spatial context prediction in natural images. Weight sharing enables higher accuracy with a small trainable parameter count. We introduce Spatial-TRM, a compact recursive model with frozen vision-language features, a convex region decoder, and just 11.2M trainable parameters. This weight-tied reasoner supports six spatial relationships, three reference frames, and open-vocabulary anchor objects. On the RoboSpatial-Home benchmark, Spatial-TRM achieves 29.51% context accuracy, a gain of 9.02 percentage points (44.0% relative) over a separately trained single-step model with the same parameter count. Including the frozen encoders, the model has 877.8M total parameters, approximately $15\times$ fewer than the reported 13B size of RoboPoint. These results show that repeated refinement improves spatial context prediction from pretrained vision-language features at a fixed trainable parameter count on this benchmark.

items.title_en: FlashReFocus: Interactive Image Refocusing in Seconds
items.abstract_en: Single-image refocusing changes the focal plane and depth of field of a photograph after capture. It is inherently interactive: users try many focal points and blur strengths on one image, so each edit should be fast and change only the blur. Recent generative methods, however, rerun large diffusion models for every edit. We observe that the two sub-problems differ in kind: recovering the all-in-focus image is ill-posed and needs a generative prior, whereas rendering blur is largely determined by depth and the focal plane. We therefore propose FlashReFocus, which runs diffusion once per photograph and renders every edit with a lightweight network. To address the ill-posed restoration, a one-step diffusion deblurrer with a decoder refiner recovers fine detail efficiently while balancing fidelity and perceptual quality. For precise control, the renderer is conditioned on an explicit defocus map and uses defocus-bias attention, which lets pixels at similar defocus share information without interference from pixels at other depths; in-focus content stays unchanged, and editing the map yields tilt-shift and two focal planes. To further test generalization to unseen cameras, we collect 3CReal, a three-camera benchmark of 89 pairs. FlashReFocus achieves the best perceptual fidelity for zero-shot bokeh rendering on EBB! and 3CReal, refocuses 148.3x faster than GenRefocus, and takes about half a second per further edit, 462x faster.

items.title_en: The Optimal Ranking Tradeoffs Between Two Ranking Scores in Two-Class Classification
items.abstract_en: The accuracy, true negative rate (negative class recall), true positive rate (positive class recall), negative predictive value (negative class precision), positive predictive value (positive class precision), class-specific intersections over unions, class-specific F-scores, Cohen's kappa, and balanced accuracy are scores that one intuitively wants to maximize when developing machine learning methods. However, they lead to different rankings of such methods. So, how can we establish a ranking that is an optimal tradeoff between any pair of these scores? It turns out that all these scores are special cases of ranking scores: a continuum of scores parameterized by the relative importance values assigned to the true negative, false positive, false negative, and true positive outcomes. Since all these scores are known to induce meaningful rankings, we seek the optimal tradeoffs among them. We consider the tradeoff between two scores to be optimal when it minimizes the Fréchet variance regarding the Kendall distance (also known as the bubble-sort distance) between rankings. For any given set of classifiers to rank, the optimal tradeoff lies at the center of the shortest (geodesic) path on the manifold of all rankings induced by the ranking scores. However, in the parameter space of the ranking scores, it is rarely achieved by averaging the importance values corresponding to the initial scores. In this paper, we present an exact analytical solution for determining a ranking score that is an optimal tradeoff for any given pair of initial scores, in the common case where the class priors are the same for all compared performances. We also experimentally investigate what happens when performance follows some distributions with fixed priors.

items.title_en: I2V-DETACH: Source Grounding Detachment for Unauthorized Image-to-Video Generation
items.abstract_en: Recent diffusion models have advanced image-conditioned video generation, but their accessibility raises risks of unauthorized manipulation. Image immunization has emerged as a promising defense for Image-to-Video (I2V) protection, yet existing methods often rely on degrading visual quality or temporal coherence. In this work, we revisit I2V immunization as reducing source-content preservation, shifting the focus from output degradation to weakening source-conditioned content propagation. To this end, we propose I2V-DETACH, an image immunization method that prevents unauthorized I2V generation through source grounding detachment. I2V models preserve source content by propagating source-image cues into video latents during denoising. Accordingly, I2V-DETACH disrupts this process in two complementary ways: it suppresses source-video grounding to reduce source cue propagation, and strengthens intra-video interactions to shift denoising toward video-side dynamics with reduced reliance on the source image. To obtain informative optimization signals, we initialize auxiliary video latents with source-oriented states that remain within the source-conditioned generation regime while deviating from source-preserving trajectories. Extensive experiments across diverse diffusion architectures show that I2V-DETACH substantially reduces source-content preservation, improves over prior immunization methods, and exhibits strong black-box transferability.

items.title_en: Xiaomi-Lens-0 Technical Report
items.abstract_en: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) answer questions about whole images well, yet they still struggle with fine-grained region understanding. A key reason is that text-only supervision never specifies which regions support an answer. To close this gap, we present Xiaomi-Lens-0, a 4B MLLM built on Qwen3.5 that predicts masks from its own visual representations. Specifically, a lightweight decoder combines vision-encoder patch features with visual latents, the language model's mask-token states, so mask supervision reaches the shared backbone without an additional segmentation encoder. Because each latent decodes to a mask, the model can interleave reasoning with region-specific latents and thus think with visual latents, while grounded reasoning traces supervise the regions it visits during chain-of-thought. As a result, across all eight RefCOCO, RefCOCO+, and RefCOCOg splits, Xiaomi-Lens-0 gains 5.6 points on average over Qwen3.5 in referring comprehension and achieves the highest segmentation cIoU among compared models. Moreover, it surpasses Qwen3.5 across all perception benchmarks. Homepage: \href{https://seerray-lab.github.io/Xiaomi-Lens-0}{this https URL}

items.title_en: Agentic Image Generation in the Wild
items.abstract_en: Agentic image generation pairs an image generator with a search agent that retrieves references from the web, extending generation beyond the generator's training data. Real-world requests, however, often concern entities that appeared only days ago. We call this setting Image Generation in the Wild. In this setting, the web offers limited visual evidence, search results are crowded with easily confused entities, and the target is rarely shown on its own. To study this setting, we build an automated pipeline that synthesizes prompts from recent headlines and keeps only those whose real search results are highly confusing, yielding requests that are hard to solve yet natural to ask. With it, we construct Savanna, a benchmark of 500 prompts across 16 subcategories. On Savanna, even harness frameworks built on the frontier models retrieve a correct reference for only about half of the prompts. We then propose Locate-Corroborate-Isolate, a paradigm in which the agent first pins down the target's identity through text search, then verifies candidate images against multiple sources, and finally crops a clean reference for the generator. Trained on 15K trajectories that follow this paradigm, Ranger-8B achieves a search score of 67.2, outperforming harnesses equipped with frontier models. It also achieves the best generation quality with every generator we test, and surpasses prior agentic methods on other image generation benchmarks. We release the pipeline, benchmark, training data and model at https://github.com/RUCAIBox/Agentic-ImageGen-Wild.

items.title_en: SCALE: Improving Guidance-Free Visual Generation via Self-Contrastive Alignment for Likelihood Estimation
items.abstract_en: Classifier-free guidance (CFG) is essential for improving sample quality in visual generation, but it incurs substantial sampling overhead. Existing guidance-free approaches halve this cost by approximating the CFG with a single model inference, but their performance is bounded by the CFG and inherits its limitations. In this paper, we propose self-contrastive guidance (SCG), which contrasts the model's prediction on real and self-generated samples to obtain a direct, model-based signal that pushes generation toward the true data manifold. Integrating SCG into the standard likelihood objective via reparameterization yields Self-Contrastive Alignment for Likelihood Estimation (SCALE), a guidance-free training framework that produces SCG-enhanced predictions in a single forward pass. Across class-conditional and text-to-image generation on diffusion and autoregressive models, SCALE consistently outperforms CFG-mimicking guidance-free baselines and improves further when combined with DPO, demonstrating that the self-contrastive signal yields gains complementary to both CFG and preference-based fine-tuning.

items.title_en: Expand-and-Prune: Test-Time Candidate-Space Adaptation for End-to-End Autonomous Driving
items.abstract_en: Candidate-based end-to-end driving planners reason over a finite set of trajectory hypotheses. However, for sparse planners, a limited candidate set may provide insufficient support for scene-relevant maneuvers, while fixed downstream candidate budgets do not account for prediction uncertainty. To address these challenges, we introduce Expand-and-Prune, a test-time framework that jointly adapts candidate support and capacity without updating learned parameters. The framework expands the native candidate set using semantic driving intent and temporally propagated predictions and then uses uncertainty in intermediate trajectory scores to adaptively prune the resulting candidates. Across four heterogeneous candidate-based planners and four benchmarks, Expand-and-Prune consistently improves planning performance. It achieves state-of-the-art results on LangAuto, increasing the Driving Score from 68.2 to 75.9, while providing further improvement on Bench2Drive, Fail2Drive, and NAVSIMv2, with particularly strong improvements in out-of-distribution scenarios. Moreover, in its full instantiation, 72.5% of selected trajectories originate from the newly introduced intent-guided or temporal candidates, confirming that candidate-space expansion provides useful hypotheses beyond those generated natively by the planner. The code is available at https://github.com/iis-esslingen/Expand-and-Prune.

items.title_en: LonGaussian: Tracking Foundation Priors for Long-Context Feedforward Gaussian Reconstruction
items.abstract_en: Reconstructing high-quality, renderable 3D scenes from long videos is essential for robotic perception and embodied intelligence. Many feed-forward Gaussian reconstruction methods rapidly predict 3D scenes from a small set of images, but extending them to longer sequences presents two bottlenecks: jointly processing all views increases GPU memory requirements, while accumulating pixel-aligned predictions redundantly represents the same surfaces and increases storage and rendering costs. We present LonGaussian, a streaming feed-forward framework that reconstructs compact, globally renderable Gaussian scenes from long image sequences with known intrinsics and unknown camera poses. Built on a pretrained streaming 3D reconstruction backbone, LonGaussian decodes long-context geometric features into dense Gaussians. Within each chunk, multi-frame point tracks link repeated observations of the same surface and guide a learned merger to consolidate the corresponding Gaussian predictions. Rendered-depth consistency filtering further suppresses Gaussians from other chunks that incorrectly occlude locally reconstructed surfaces. On DL3DV and RealEstate10K benchmarks, LonGaussian improves novel-view rendering quality while using substantially fewer Gaussians than the evaluated feed-forward baselines.

items.title_en: Can the Parts Fool the Test? Counterfactual Pairing Cycles for Relational OOD
items.abstract_en: Relational out-of-distribution errors are easy to describe and hard to evaluate cleanly. An image may be natural, a caption may be fluent, and all mentioned objects may be common, yet the caption may describe the wrong relation in the image. Many evaluations intended to test this behavior can be solved without checking the pairing at all, because negatives differ in caption style, template, length, object frequency, or image statistics. We propose counterfactual pairing cycles, a blocked evaluation primitive that reuses the same two images and the same two captions on both sides of the comparison, changing only which image is paired with which caption. This makes image-only, text-only, and additive component shortcuts cancel exactly in finite samples. The same contrast also gives a training loss for relational outlier exposure and a diagnostic for bilinear vision-language scores. Across synthetic controls, GQA, and COCO, cycles separate coarse image-caption matching from directional role-binding failures, while also identifying geometric size relations that remain strongly visible in global features. In a shortcut-contaminated COCO outlier-exposure stress test, a model selected by a near-perfect shortcut validation AUROC retains substantial relational signal but remains below cycle training on exact cycles; cycle training improves CycleAcc from 0.882 to 0.927. The main lesson is simple: to test whether a model understands a pairing, the benchmark should keep the parts fixed, change the pairing, and ask only about coupling. The official implementation is available online.

items.title_en: Kingfisher: Fast Personalized Visual Autoregressive Generation via Scale-Aware Prompt-Conditioned Scale Decomposition
items.abstract_en: Personalized image generation has been extensively studied in diffusion models, often relying on subject-specific optimization of model weights, textual embeddings, LoRA modules, or adapters. In this work, we explore a different direction for fast personalization in visual autoregressive models. Our key observation is that a short prefix of early autoregressive scale codes is sufficient to strongly determine both object structure and global appearance, while later scales primarily refine the established generation trajectory. Based on this insight, we introduce Kingfisher, a model-tuning-free framework that decomposes early residual scale codes into content- and style-related components through prompt-conditioned scale-code subspaces. Given two real images, Kingfisher first decomposes their early scale codes, then recomposes the content components of one image with the style components of the other into a compact semantic prefix. The frozen generator subsequently predicts the remaining scales through bitwise self-correction for coherent refinement. Experiments on CSD-100 show that Kingfisher achieves strong content preservation and the highest style and text alignment among the evaluated methods, while reducing pair-specific preparation time by approximately 54x compared with diffusion-based methods and 7.5x compared with VAR-based alternatives. These results demonstrate that effective personalization can be achieved by directly manipulating the native scale-space representation of a frozen visual autoregressive generator.

items.title_en: CXCL9-Dependent Immune Networks of Spontaneous Tertiary Lymphoid Structures in a Murine Subcutaneous Tumor Model
items.title_zh: 小鼠皮下肿瘤模型中自发三级淋巴结构的 CXCL9 依赖免疫网络
items.abstract_en: Recent discoveries have identified human tumor tertiary lymphoid structures (TLS) as organized clusters of innate and adaptive immune cells and stromal cells. Cancer-associated TLS can promote tumor clearance and enhance responses to immune checkpoint blockade (ICB) immunotherapy. However, the absence of TLS in conventional mouse tumor models, particularly subcutaneous transplant models, limits experimental manipulation and study of TLS development. By tuning tumor antigen expression, we have generated a subcutaneous tumor model that naturally forms TLS within the immune-hot, vasculature-rich peritumoral adipose tissue. These TLS were identified as clusters of B and T cells in close proximity to high endothelial venules. TLS organization was underpinned by spatially compartmentalized chemokine expression, with CCL21 produced in the T cell zone of perivascular TLS and CXCL13 present in the B cell region. Single cell transcriptomic sequencing showed that the immune composition in the TLS forming peritumoral tissue resembled human cancer TLS signatures. Upon anti-PD-L1 ICB treatment, TLS underwent expansion, which was associated with increased interferon responses in macrophages and coincided with tumor clearance. We further identified the interferon-inducible chemokine CXCL9 as a key regulator of the TLS microenvironment. CXCL9-expressing macrophages populated TLS, interacting with B cells following ICB treatment. CXCL9 deficiency reduced B cell recruitment to peritumoral tissue and TLS formation. Further T and B cell receptor sequencing indicated a CXCL9-dependent promotion of antigen-specific responses within the tumor and TLS niche. Combined, these findings establish a tractable subcutaneous model of naturally arising tumor TLS and define the cellular and molecular networks that regulate their formation and function. This provides a platform to dissect how TLS develop and test strategies that promote TLS formation to enhance cancer therapy.
items.abstract_zh: 人类肿瘤三级淋巴结构（TLS）是由先天免疫、适应性免疫细胞与基质细胞组成的有组织细胞簇，可促进肿瘤清除并增强免疫检查点阻断（ICB）疗效。但常规小鼠肿瘤模型，尤其皮下移植模型，缺乏 TLS，限制了对其发育的实验研究。通过调节肿瘤抗原表达，我们构建了一个在免疫活跃、血管丰富的瘤周脂肪组织中自发形成 TLS 的皮下肿瘤模型。这些 TLS 是紧邻高内皮微静脉的 B、T 细胞聚集体，其组织依赖空间分隔的趋化因子表达：血管周 TLS 的 T 细胞区产生 CCL21，B 细胞区存在 CXCL13。单细胞转录组测序显示，形成 TLS 的瘤周组织免疫组成类似人类癌症 TLS 特征。抗 PD-L1 治疗后 TLS 扩增，伴随巨噬细胞干扰素反应增强，并与肿瘤清除同步。我们进一步发现，干扰素诱导趋化因子 CXCL9 是 TLS 微环境的关键调控因子：表达 CXCL9 的巨噬细胞填充 TLS，并在 ICB 后与 B 细胞相互作用；CXCL9 缺失会减少 B 细胞向瘤周组织募集及 TLS 形成。T、B 细胞受体测序进一步表明，CXCL9 依赖性地促进肿瘤与 TLS 微环境中的抗原特异性反应。
items.highlight_zh: 建立自发形成 TLS 的皮下瘤模型，锁定 CXCL9 为关键调控因子
items.digest_zh:
1. 研究问题：三级淋巴结构（TLS）是肿瘤内由免疫细胞和基质细胞组成的“临时淋巴结”，与更好的免疫治疗响应相关。但常用的小鼠皮下移植瘤几乎不长 TLS，导致很难在实验中研究它是怎么形成的、受什么调控。
2. 方法：作者通过调节肿瘤抗原的表达强度，筛出一个能在瘤周脂肪组织中自发形成 TLS 的皮下肿瘤模型；随后用单细胞转录组测序、趋化因子空间定位、T/B 细胞受体测序以及抗 PD-L1 治疗等手段，解析其细胞组成与分子机制，并检验 CXCL9 的作用。
3. 结果：这些 TLS 是紧邻高内皮微静脉的 B、T 细胞聚集体，T 细胞区有 CCL21、B 细胞区有 CXCL13，免疫组成与人类肿瘤 TLS 特征相似。抗 PD-L1 治疗后 TLS 扩大，伴随巨噬细胞干扰素反应增强，并与肿瘤消退同步。表达 CXCL9 的巨噬细胞填充 TLS，并在治疗后与 B 细胞互作；CXCL9 缺失会减少 B 细胞募集与 TLS 形成，也削弱肿瘤及 TLS 内的抗原特异性反应。
4. 意义：提供了一个可实验操作、自发形成 TLS 的小鼠模型，并把 CXCL9 确立为 TLS 微环境的关键调控节点，为提升免疫检查点阻断疗效提供潜在靶点。

items.title_en: IL-2 and CD40L can establish and sustain a human B cell-mediated immune regulatory network
items.title_zh: IL-2 与 CD40L 可建立并维持人 B 细胞介导的免疫调控网络
items.abstract_en: B cells can control inflammation, but the factors governing B cell-mediated immune regulatory network remain unclear. We report that IL-2/CD40L enable class-switched memory (CSM) B cells to acquire an immunosuppressive phenotype characterized by the expression of surface TIGIT as well as multiple other inhibitory receptors (PD-1, LAG-3, GITR, CD39, and CTLA-4) and soluble molecules (IL-10, granzyme B, and IL-35). TIGIT+ CSM B cells expressing functional CCR9 exhibit significant defects in total immunoglobulin secretion, while preserving IgA2 secretion. Furthermore, IL-2/CD40L-induced ex vivo-generated TIGIT+ CSM B cells suppress human T cell-mediated inflammation in a xenogeneic mouse model of acute graft-versus-host disease, while promoting IL-10-producing regulatory T cell (Treg) response. These findings identify IL-2/CD40L as key drivers of a B cell-mediated immune regulatory network, especially by generating TIGIT+ CSM B cells that can further promote Treg response. This study supports the development of TIGIT+ B cell-based therapy models for inflammatory diseases.
items.abstract_zh: B 细胞能够控制炎症，但决定 B 细胞介导免疫调控网络的因素仍不清楚。本研究发现，IL-2/CD40L 可使类别转换记忆（CSM）B 细胞获得免疫抑制表型：表面表达 TIGIT 以及 PD-1、LAG-3、GITR、CD39、CTLA-4 等多种抑制性受体，并分泌 IL-10、颗粒酶 B 和 IL-35 等可溶性分子。表达功能性 CCR9 的 TIGIT+ CSM B 细胞总免疫球蛋白分泌显著受损，但保留 IgA2 分泌。此外，IL-2/CD40L 诱导的体外生成 TIGIT+ CSM B 细胞可在急性移植物抗宿主病异种小鼠模型中抑制人 T 细胞介导的炎症，同时促进产生 IL-10 的调节性 T 细胞（Treg）应答。这些结果提示 IL-2/CD40L 是 B 细胞免疫调控网络的关键驱动因素，并支持开发基于 TIGIT+ B 细胞的炎症性疾病治疗策略。
items.highlight_zh: IL-2/CD40L 驱动 TIGIT+ 记忆 B 细胞构建免疫抑制网络
items.digest_zh:
【研究问题】B 细胞通常被视为抗体工厂，但越来越多证据显示部分 B 细胞还能给免疫反应“踩刹车”。究竟是什么信号把这些 B 细胞训练成抑制性细胞，此前并不清楚。
【方法】研究者在体外用 IL-2 与 CD40L 联合刺激人的类别转换记忆（CSM）B 细胞，系统检测其表面抑制性受体和分泌分子的变化；同时分析其中表达 CCR9、TIGIT 的亚群在抗体分泌上的特点；并在人源化急性移植物抗宿主病（GVHD）异种小鼠模型中检验这些细胞能否抑制人 T 细胞引起的炎症。
【结果】IL-2/CD40L 刺激后的 CSM B 细胞同时上调 TIGIT、PD-1、LAG-3、GITR、CD39、CTLA-4 等抑制性受体，并分泌 IL-10、颗粒酶 B、IL-35；这些 TIGIT+ 细胞总体免疫球蛋白分泌下降，却保留了 IgA2 的分泌，提示其功能被“选择性重编程”。在 GVHD 小鼠中，体外诱导出的 TIGIT+ CSM B 细胞能显著压制 T 细胞介导的炎症，并促进产 IL-10 的 Treg 扩增。
【意义】该工作把 IL-2/CD40L 确立为 B 细胞免疫调控网络的关键开关，并说明 TIGIT+ B 细胞可以“再招募”Treg 形成放大回路。这为炎症性疾病提供了新的细胞治疗思路：不必只压制 T 细胞，也可以主动扩增这类具有抑制功能的 B 细胞。

items.title_en: A CAR T cell-amplified suppressive B cell circuit in AML
items.title_zh: 急性髓系白血病中由 CAR T 细胞放大的抑制性 B 细胞环路
items.abstract_en: Immunotherapy in acute myeloid leukemia (AML) is constrained by a hostile bone marrow niche. Here we identify atypical memory B cells (Batyp) as a suppressive population within this microenvironment. Across single cell and flow cytometry cohorts, Batyp were expanded in AML, and their molecular and phenotypic profiles resembled those of atypical B cells associated with chronic inflammatory conditions. Batyp were polarized within the AML microenvironment, and this was amplified by CAR T cell-AML interactions. Mechanistically, polarization was dependent on Toll-like receptor, interferon and CD70-CD27 signaling. Batyp suppressed T cell and CAR T cell responses via PD-1- and TGF-beta signaling, and were enriched in non-responding patients with AML and myeloma. CD180-directed CAR T cells, targeting an antigen shared by Batyp and AML blasts, resisted suppression in vitro and cleared disease in B cell-humanized xenografts while sparing hematopoietic stem cells, with B cell engagement further enhancing their expansion. CAR T cells thus reinforce their own suppressive niche through Batyp polarization, a constraint that can be relieved by dual blast- and B cell-targeting strategies.
items.abstract_zh: 急性髓系白血病（AML）的免疫治疗受制于敌对的骨髓微环境。本研究在该微环境中鉴定出一群非典型记忆 B 细胞（Batyp）作为抑制性细胞群。跨单细胞与流式细胞术队列分析显示，Batyp 在 AML 中扩增，其分子与表型特征类似慢性炎症相关非典型 B 细胞。Batyp 在 AML 微环境内被极化，且 CAR T 细胞与 AML 细胞的相互作用会进一步放大这一过程；机制上，极化依赖 Toll 样受体、干扰素及 CD70-CD27 信号。Batyp 通过 PD-1 与 TGF-β 信号抑制 T 细胞和 CAR T 细胞应答，并在 AML 与骨髓瘤无应答患者中富集。靶向 Batyp 与 AML 原始细胞共有抗原 CD180 的 CAR T 细胞在体外可抵抗抑制，在 B 细胞人源化异种移植中清除疾病且不损伤造血干细胞，与 B 细胞结合还进一步增强其扩增。因此，CAR T 细胞会通过 Batyp 极化加固自身所处的抑制性生态位，而同时靶向原始细胞与 B 细胞的双靶策略可解除这一限制。
items.highlight_zh: CAR T 细胞反而放大 B 细胞抑制环路，双靶策略可破解
items.digest_zh:
【研究问题】AML 的免疫治疗（包括 CAR T）效果有限，常被归因于骨髓微环境“敌对”。但这种敌对状态由哪些细胞造成、能否被干预，仍不清楚。
【方法】作者整合单细胞测序与流式细胞术队列，比较 AML 患者与对照的 B 细胞亚群；在体外和体内验证这群非典型记忆 B 细胞（Batyp）如何被极化、又如何抑制 T 细胞；通过阻断 Toll 样受体、干扰素和 CD70-CD27 信号确定机制；进而设计靶向 CD180（Batyp 与 AML 原始细胞共有抗原）的 CAR T 细胞，并在 B 细胞人源化异种移植模型中评估疗效与安全性。
【结果】Batyp 在 AML 中显著扩增，其表型类似慢性炎症中的非典型 B 细胞；AML 微环境会使其向抑制性方向极化，而 CAR T 细胞与白血病细胞的相互作用会进一步放大这一极化。Batyp 通过 PD-1 与 TGF-β 信号压制普通 T 细胞和 CAR T 细胞，并在 AML、骨髓瘤治疗无应答患者中富集。靶向 CD180 的 CAR T 在体外能抵抗这种抑制，在体内清除肿瘤且不伤害造血干细胞；与 B 细胞结合反而促进其自身扩增。
【意义】这项研究提示一个值得警惕的悖论：CAR T 细胞在杀伤肿瘤的同时，可能亲手强化压制自己的 B 细胞生态位。把白血病原始细胞和 Batyp 一起作为靶点，可能成为提升 AML 免疫治疗疗效的可行设计原则。

items.title_en: Sustained antigenic engagement programs multidimensional CTL states with distinct cytotoxic capacities
items.title_zh: 持续抗原接合程序化具有不同细胞毒性能力的多维 CTL 状态
items.abstract_en: Cytotoxic T lymphocytes (CTLs) eliminate infected or malignant cells through repeated target-cell encounters, yet how they sustain cytotoxic activity during extended antigenic stimulation remains poorly understood. In particular, it remains unclear whether preserved population-level killing reflects maintenance of a uniform effector phenotype or diversification into functionally distinct CTL populations. Here, we combined live-cell imaging, high-dimensional cytometry, single-cell RNA sequencing, phenotypic trajectory analysis, population sorting, and rechallenge killing assays to define how human clonal CTLs remodel during sustained antigenic engagement. Prior antigen encounter altered the kinetics and pattern of target-cell membrane permeabilization but did not compromise overall subsequent killing upon rechallenge. Single-cell transcriptomic profiling after prolonged engagement revealed broad remodeling of antigen-experienced CTLs and heterogeneous cytotoxic transcriptional programs. Time-resolved scRNA-seq further showed that these functional dimensions remodeled with distinct kinetics, with rapid induction of activation- and cytotoxicity-associated programs, later remodeling of vesicular-trafficking programs, and progressive reduction of adhesion/ contact interaction -associated programs. High-dimensional cytometry showed that this temporal remodeling was accompanied by progressive redistribution of CTLs across a multidimensional protein-expression landscape defined by distinct combinations of cytotoxic, vesicular/degranulation, activation, cytokine, adhesion, and regulatory features. Phenotypic trajectory analysis organized this protein landscape along a temporal remodeling axis, with early lytic-granule-rich profiles giving way to multiple late-engaged phenotypes with distinct combinations of functional protein features. Surface-marker-defined late CTL populations displayed distinct killing capacities upon rechallenge, demonstrating that preserved population-level cytotoxicity can coexist with substantial functional heterogeneity. Finally, CAR T cells exposed to CD19+ targets retained cytotoxic activity upon rechallenge and acquired multidimensional phenotypic features that partially overlapped with the remodeling framework identified in clonal CTLs. Reanalysis of longitudinal patient-derived CAR T-cell transcriptomes further showed that related functional programs were dynamically organized after infusion, with the features distinguishing responder and non-responder tisa-cel samples changing between the infusion product and day 7. Together, these findings indicate that sustained CTL killing is accompanied by progressive multidimensional remodeling and diversification rather than maintenance of a fixed effector phenotype. Our findings support a model in which population-level cytotoxic activity can be maintained while the CTLs composing that population progressively diversify into functionally distinct states during sustained antigenic engagement.

items.title_en: Alternative splicing use ratio is not conserved between human and mouse immune cells
items.title_zh: 可变剪接使用比例在人与小鼠免疫细胞间不保守
items.abstract_en: Most human genes have mouse orthologs. However, orthology at the level of exons and alternative splicing events is not well defined, and the use of alternative splicing events in immune cell types has not been compared between human and mouse. We mapped exons and alternative splicing events between human and mouse. Based on this mapping, the use ratio of orthologous alternative splicing events was compared between human and mouse immune cell types and fibroblasts. Out of the 1,823 human-mouse orthologous alternative splicing events that are expressed in the five tested immune cell types, most (62-67%) showed a significant difference in use ratio between human and mouse, and less than third (21-25%) retained the same ratio. Our results reveal both conserved and divergent alternative splicing usage ratio, and highlight the dynamic evolution of alternative splicing regulation across human and mouse immune cell types. By integrating exon orthology with observed splicing patterns, our analysis provides a functional framework for studying mammalian splicing ratio evolution beyond static transcript annotations.

items.title_en: Stage-specific checkpoint signalling by ATM, ATR and DNA-PK safeguards oocyte genome integrity
items.title_zh: ATM、ATR 和 DNA-PK 的阶段特异性检查点信号保障卵母细胞基因组完整性
items.abstract_en: In somatic cells, DNA double-strand breaks (DSBs) are potentially catastrophic lesions that activate phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase-related kinase (PIKK) signalling to promote DNA repair or eliminate damaged cells. During meiosis, however, DSBs are deliberately generated as essential intermediates in homologous recombination, raising the question of how DNA damage signalling distinguishes programmed recombination from genome instability. To define how PIKK signalling is adapted to these distinct contexts, we resolved the function of the three PIKKs ATM, ATR and DNA-PK in physiological meiotic recombination and the response to postnatal DNA damage in mouse oocytes. Following postnatal irradiation, ATM functions as the dominant response kinase, with ATR and DNA-PK acting redundantly to eliminate damaged oocytes. In contrast, meiotic surveillance is mediated by ATR, with ATR removal rescuing oocyte loss in response to asynapsis and, independently, to persistent meiotic DSBs. Unexpectedly, depletion of ATR fails to rescue constitutive Atm-null oocytes, while co-depletion of ATR and DNA-PK results in only partial rescue, revealing a PIKK-independent mechanism of oocyte elimination. Our findings demonstrate that DNA damage signalling is developmentally reconfigured during oogenesis and highlight distinct pathways of oocyte elimination that may ultimately inform strategies to maintain the ovarian reserve in mammals.

items.title_en: cBAF drives AR-V7 expression through regulation of transcriptional termination in castration-resistant prostate cancer
items.title_zh: cBAF 通过调控转录终止驱动去势抵抗性前列腺癌中的 AR-V7 表达
items.abstract_en: The androgen receptor splice variant AR-V7 drives resistance to androgen receptor-targeted therapies in castration-resistant prostate cancer (CRPC), but the mechanisms governing its expression remain incompletely understood. Here, we identify the canonical BAF (cBAF) chromatin remodeling complex as a selective regulator of AR-V7 expression. Pharmacologic and genetic disruption of cBAF reduced AR-V7 levels, suppressed AR-V7-dependent transcriptional programs, and impaired CRPC cell proliferation. Mechanistically, cBAF binds an intronic regulatory element downstream of AR cryptic exon 3, where it maintains chromatin accessibility, enhancer activity, and promoter-enhancer looping. cBAF loss decreases recruitment of transcription termination machinery, reduces RNA polymerase II Thr4 phosphorylation, and promotes transcriptional readthrough beyond the AR-V7 polyadenylation site. POINT-seq revealed that cBAF-dependent transcriptional termination is required for AR-V7 biogenesis and regulates termination at a subset of genes genome-wide. Together, these findings uncover a role for cBAF in chromatin-mediated control of transcriptional termination and establish this mechanism as a critical determinant of AR-V7 expression.

items.title_en: Thille, a chromosome-level type B avocado genome, and the structural and allelic variation at candidate flowering-type loci
items.title_zh: Thille：一个染色体水平的 B 型鳄梨基因组，以及候选开花型位点的结构和等位变异
items.abstract_en: Avocado (Persea americana Mill.) is heterodichogamous: each flower opens first as female and then as male, and cultivars fall into two complementary flowering types, A and B, determined by the transcription factor SDMYB, whose dominant allele confers type A. Avocado genomes have so far come from type A cultivars. Here we report a chromosome-level genome of Thille, a type B cultivar used in breeding. From 72.2 Gb of PacBio HiFi reads (81x coverage) and Omni-C data, the assembly places 859.8 Mb, 96% of the expected 896 Mb genome, in 12 chromosomes with an NG50 of 84.5 Mb, a consensus quality of QV 69.95, and 97.3% complete BUSCO genes; repeats occupy 64.0% of the assembly, and 35,386 protein-coding genes were predicted. We compared Thille with the type A cultivars Hass and Puebla, a predominantly Guatemalan hybrid, and with a West Indian (WI) accession, a Lowland botanical group variety of unreported flowering type. The assemblies differ by large rearrangements, including an 18.8 Mb inversion on chromosome 12 specific to Hass. Using phased reads and haplotype assemblies, we reconstructed the alleles of candidate flowering genes from a type A versus type B Fst scan. Both WI haplotypes carry the recessive SDMYB allele found in Thille; based on this study and the previous study of SDMYB, we predict the WI accession to be type B. Six genes, including SDMYB, carry an allele shared by all three type A cultivars and absent from Thille and WI. The genome and HiFi reads are available under BioProject PRJNA1142556.

items.title_en: Camouflage functions of juvenile giant panda colouration in forest environments
items.title_zh: 幼年大熊猫体色在森林环境中的伪装功能
items.abstract_en: The contrasting black-and-white coloration of the giant panda (Ailuropoda melanoleuca) has long attracted attention. Recent works suggest this contrasting pattern may generate camouflage-relevant visual effects. However, most previous studies have focused on adult pandas, whereas juveniles may face greater predation risk and may therefore represent a more ecologically relevant life stage for testing concealment hypotheses. We investigated whether juvenile panda coloration provides the potential for camouflage through background matching or disruptive coloration, and how this potential is shaped by vegetation cover, illumination and background position. We used life-sized juvenile panda models with natural and experimentally modified coloration by adjusting the relative proportions and spatial arrangement of white, black, and grey patches. Models were photographed in temperate woodland environments at ground level and against canopy backgrounds, under sunny and cloudy conditions, with and without vegetation occlusion. We quantified colour and luminance contrast, as well as edge-disruption metrics, using dichromatic canid and felid visual models. Natural juvenile panda coloration influences target-background contrast and edge-disruption, although these effects varies with vegetation, lighting, background height and visual model. Vegetation cover significantly reduced contrast and increased edge disruption metrics, while bright light condition only increased the metrics of edge disruption. Background position affected camouflage-relevant metrics in a context- and observer-dependent manner: under vegetation occlusion, canopy placement reduced chromatic contrast under felid-like vision, whereas ground-level placement reduced luminance contrast under both visual models. Alterations to patch extent and boundary arrangement modified camouflage-relevant metrics under specific environmental conditions, suggesting that the natural arrangement of pelage boundaries may enhance concealment under specific conditions. Overall, our findings support the hypothesis that juvenile giant panda coloration can produce visual effects consistent with potential camouflage, while highlighting the importance of habitat structure and viewing context in shaping camouflage.

items.title_en: RiboBridge couples RNA backbone generation to sequence design through a learned interaction topology
items.title_zh: RiboBridge 通过学习到的相互作用拓扑将 RNA 骨架生成与序列设计耦合
items.abstract_en: Designing ribonucleic acid (RNA) molecules with prescribed structures and functions is central to RNA engineering. Backbone-first approaches generate three-dimensional geometry before assigning a nucleotide sequence, yet leave open how that geometry should be represented for downstream sequence design. Here we introduce RiboBridge, which infers a probabilistic residue-pair state from backbone geometry, recycles binary pair probabilities through a second pass and transfers binary and typed signals as soft attention biases for sequence decoding. On 550 generated backbones, pair-type decoding achieved joint refolding validity of 0.451 versus 0.335 for an architecture-matched topology-free decoder. On a matched 110-backbone intervention cohort, replacing aligned pair states with exact-length donors matched on pair-state statistics reduced joint validity from 0.464 to 0.214, showing backbone alignment matters. Pair-confidence ranking enriched the joint-validity rate from 0.451 overall to 0.596 among the top 248 before external refolding, with the same ranking signal transferring to independently generated RFDpoly and RNA-FrameFlow backbones. On 53 experimentally determined backbones, pair-coupled decoding improved secondary-structure agreement relative to residue-wise argmax. These results support a learned relational interface between sequence-free backbone generation and sequence design.

items.title_en: Metalink: Joint taxonomic and functional profiling of metagenomes and metatranscriptomes across resolution scales
items.title_zh: Metalink：跨分辨率尺度的宏基因组与宏转录组联合分类学和功能解析
items.abstract_en: Metagenomic and metatranscriptomic analyses remain largely fragmented: taxonomic and functional profiling are performed separately, often at a single resolution (reads, contigs, or MAGs) yielding separate species or function lists rather than mechanistic insights. Here, we developed Metalink, a tool that unifies taxonomic and functional profiling into coupled outputs across all three resolution levels. Metalink is built on three innovations. First, we constructed a Last Common Function-based functional Hierarchy (LCFH) from ~424 million proteins, organizing KEGG Orthologs into a tree structure that enables LCA-like functional assignment. Second, a unified framework integrates the taxonomy of Genome Taxonomy Database (GTDB), the International Committee on Taxonomy of Viruses (ICTV), and NCBI for consistent classification across reads, contigs, and MAGs. Third, a multi-level integration strategy with overlap-based deduplication balances accuracy and completeness. At the read level, Metalink exceeds both HUMAnN3 and eggNOG-Mapper in functional assignment accuracy while running ~30-fold faster and 1,000-fold faster, respectively; at the contig level, its functional profiles remain highly consistent with eggNOG-Mapper. Multi-level integration further improves taxonomic resolution over single-level analyses and outperforms leading taxonomic profilers on the CAMI II benchmarks. Metalink's joint outputs move the analysis of metagenomes and metatranscriptomes from cataloging species and functions toward mechanistic inference of species-function-environment triadic associations. By enabling these integrated analyses across resolution scales, Metalink provides a general framework for linking community composition to its functional potential across diverse ecosystems.

items.title_en: Distance-AF Multimer: A Multi-Step Approach for Protein Complex Structure Modeling with User-Defined Distance Constraints
items.title_zh: Distance-AF Multimer：一种带用户定义距离约束的蛋白质复合物结构建模多步方法
items.abstract_en: The three-dimensional structure of proteins provides essential insight into the molecular mechanisms underlying their function. Many biological activities are mediated through protein interactions, making accurate structural determination of protein complexes important. Despite significant advances in computational protein structure prediction, there are still many cases where protein complexes are not correctly assembled. In particular, there are cases where experimental data, such as distances between residue pairs in interacting proteins are available, yet existing prediction methods fail to produce models consistent with these data. Here, we present Distance-AF Multimer, a method that guides and refines AlphaFold-Multimer docking predictions using user-provided residue pair distance information. This approach extends our previously successful data-guided single-protein modeling method, Distance-AF. Distance-AF Multimer operates in a two-step process, starting from multiple initial conformations and iteratively refining them to satisfy the provided distance constraints. We evaluated Distance-AF Multimer on protein-complex benchmarks spanning different chain counts and docking errors, demonstrating competitive or superior performance compared to other existing deep-learning-based structure prediction methods. In addition to dimer cases, we also demonstrated the potential of Distance-AF Multimer for large-scale protein assemblies containing multiple chains, including those with more than 5 chains.

items.title_en: An integrated database of ion channels
items.title_zh: 离子通道整合数据库
items.abstract_en: Ion channels play critical roles in a wide range of physiological processes, including the propagation of nerve impulses, insulin secretion and regulation of heart rate. Alterations in ion-channels function or expression can contribute to the development of various diseases, including cancers, genetic disorders, and infectious diseases. Ion channels represent the second-largest class of membrane proteins considered potential targets for therapeutic intervention. However, a comprehensive data resource integrating information on human ion channels and their associations with diseases has been limited. Therefore, the Integrated Database of Ion Channels (IDIC) was developed, comprising information on 493 human ion channels. The database contains a broad range of ion-channel annotations, including gene and protein information, structural details, protein signature sequences, protein domains, nuclear localization signals, and signal peptides. It also provides cross-references to several established biological resources, including the Human Genome Organization Gene Nomenclature Committee (HGNC), National Center for Biotechnology Information (NCBI) Gene, Vertebrate Genome Annotation (VEGA), Ensembl, and the Protein Data Bank (PDB). Furthermore, IDIC incorporates genomic variations identified in various tumors and disease associations involving ion channels, which have been systematically curated from published literature. Through concise search methods and user-friendly browsing functionalities, IDIC serves as an integrated resource for exploring human ion channels and investigating their structural, functional, genetic, and disease-related characteristics. Thus, the database can facilitate a better understanding of ion channels and their potential involvement in diverse human diseases.

items.title_en: Hierarchical distribution matching enables comprehensive characterization of common and condition-specific cell niches in spatial omics data
items.title_zh: 分层分布匹配可实现空间组学数据中常见与条件特异性细胞生态位的全面表征
items.abstract_en: Deciphering cell niches in complex tissues is essential for understanding tissue structure and disease. Recent advances in spatial omics have enabled subcellular resolution and accurate cell identity mapping. However, robust delineation of cell niches and disease-associated spatial patterns remains difficult. We introduce Harmonics, a novel computational framework that systematically identifies both common and condition-specific cell niches from spatial omics data through hierarchical distribution matching. Harmonics also includes a suite of downstream modules that facilitate comprehensive niche characterization. We demonstrate its scalability, accuracy and generalizability across datasets spanning diverse species, tissues, diseases, spatial modalities, and technological platforms. For condition-agnostic datasets, Harmonics outperforms baseline methods in both accuracy and robustness, and further demonstrates the capability to resolve niche structures at finer granularity. Across diverse diseases including pulmonary fibrosis, triple-negative breast cancer, and colorectal cancer, Harmonics enables precise identification of condition-specific niches and reveals disease-associated dynamics, subtype-specific spatial patterns, and structured immune architectures. We envision Harmonics as a practical and versatile tool for spatial niche analysis that can be applied across a wide range of biological contexts and seamlessly integrated with existing spatial omics workflows.

items.title_en: Latent-Factor Stability Is Not Sufficient: Evaluating SABLE-MO in Simulated and Cancer Multi-Omics Data
items.title_zh: 潜因子稳定性并不充分：在模拟与癌症多组学数据中评估 SABLE-MO
items.abstract_en: Reproducibility is often used to assess latent factors learned from multi-omics data. Yet factors that recur across model refits may not reflect the shared biological structure of interest. We investigated this issue using SABLE-MO, a shared/private representation-learning framework with a sep-arate factor-retention procedure. We evaluated the method in simulations with known latent structure. The original retention rule produced no false biological shared-factor acceptance across 800 independent-null datasets, but accepted at least one false factor in 70 of 200 correlated-private datasets (35%). Following an exploratory analysis of this failure, we increased the lower-decile aligned-correlation threshold from 0.40 to 0.60 and tested it on a new, independently seeded simulation bank. False acceptance decreased from 33% to 19%, while recovery of true shared factors changed only slightly (94.375% to 94.0%). Exact modality-support attribution reached 67.5%, below its prespecified criterion. We also analyzed matched RNA expression, DNA methylation, and copy- number data from TARGET osteosarcoma (78 patients), TCGA-SARC (250), and TCGA-KIRC (304). Outcome-blind model selec- tion favored a simpler shared/private representation in TARGET.In both TCGA cohorts, the more complex representation improved cross-view retrieval and missing-view reconstruction relative to the simpler model, but worsened ordinary reconstruction. These external comparisons were performed before factor retention. Our results show that factor reproducibility, representation quality,and biological interpretation require separate assessment. Stricter retention reduced errors in a specific simulated setting but did not eliminate them

items.title_en: Free-Energy and Molecular Dynamics Analysis of Ser195 and Thr195 Rotameric States in Thrombin
items.title_zh: 凝血酶中 Ser195 和 Thr195 旋转异构态的自由能与分子动力学分析
items.abstract_en: Ser195 is highly conserved as the catalytic nucleophile in trypsin like serine proteases, yet the molecular basis for the strong preference for serine over the chemically similar threonine residue remains unclear. Here, we used well tempered metadynamics and microsecond long molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to characterize the conformational energetics of S195 and T195 in thrombin. Well tempered metadynamics revealed distinct rotameric free energy landscapes in both the apo and the ligand bound systems. In the apo state, S195 preferentially occupied a lower angle rotameric state, while T195 exhibited two low energy states with similar free energies. Unbiased simulations further showed greater conformational heterogeneity and increased higher angle sampling for T195. Evaluation of the His57 to residue 195 hydrogen bond further revealed that S195 maintained close hydrogen bond distances across both rotameric regions, whereas T195 exhibited longer and more variable His57 to hydroxyl distances with reduced distance based occupancy. Analysis of the local environment showed that the additional T195 methyl group was associated with redistributed protein contacts. Additional rotamer conditioned analyses demonstrated differences in local packing within corresponding conformational states. Furthermore, solvent accessibility and water contact analyses revealed that the effects of the substitution on the catalytic side chain environment depend on rotameric conformation. Together, these findings demonstrate that two complementary simulation approaches converge on similar conformational preferences and suggest that the S195T substitution alters the rotameric free energy landscape in association with changes in catalytic geometry, local packing, and solvation. These results provide insight into the evolutionary preference for serine over threonine at the catalytic position of thrombin.

items.title_en: Pleiotropy links host axes of defense against a pathogen
items.title_zh: 多效性将宿主抵御病原体的防御轴联系起来
items.abstract_en: Organisms face ubiquitous threats from pathogens, and in response hosts have evolved a cascade of defenses to avoid, resist, or tolerate infection. While these stepwise defenses may act independently, they can be pleiotropically linked via shared molecular mechanisms, regulation, and crosstalk. Here, we tested the extent to which pleiotropy shapes multiple axes of defense using knockouts of 16 single genes involved in innate immunity of Caenorhabditis elegans against the opportunistic bacterial pathogen Pseudomonas aeruginosa. Host genotype had variable effects on components of host defense. Traits such as infection-induced mortality and body size varied frequently across host genotypes, while behavioral avoidance, bacterial uptake, and susceptibility to bacterial colonization varied less frequently. Broadly, pleiotropy between defenses was common, driving patterns of variation that linked several traits together. However, important components of defense like mortality, avoidance, and susceptibility to colonization were more independent from one another. Our results show that pleiotropy between defenses can be common, highlighting the importance of moving beyond single phenotypes to understand multiple dimensions of host-pathogen interactions.

items.title_en: Chain of Structures: Connecting Reasoning and Generation for Protein Design
items.title_zh: Chain of Structures：连接蛋白质设计中的推理与生成
items.abstract_en: Scientific design requires reasoning in scientific spaces that represent the objects being designed. Building on Scinetics' Chain of Science Tokens, we present chain-of-structures (COS) as a concrete protein-design case study that connects reasoning and generation through explicit structural states. In this technical report, we apply COS to enzyme design, where catalytic function requires precise local geometry within a compatible global fold, making it a demanding test of reasoning from chemical requirements to protein structure. Starting from a reaction specification and target length, COS couples a language reasoning expert with an all-atom generation expert across four rounds: catalytic core, active site, global backbone, and complete sequence and structure. Each reasoning state directly conditions generation, and the resulting structure becomes context for the next decision. Discrete residue constraints and continuous latents connect the two experts, enabling structural supervision of the reasoning interface. On the evaluated benchmark, COS leads the compared baselines on five of six metrics, achieving 57.0% EC3 agreement and a TM-score of 0.729.

items.title_en: Protein Crowding Buffers Membrane Fluidity
items.abstract_en: Like cholesterol, protein crowding has been shown to alter the temperature dependence of lateral diffusion in biomembranes, eventually eliminating the distinct liquid-gel phase transition. Here, we resolve the molecular origin of this protein effect with coarse-grained and all-atom simulations of protein-crowded phosphatidylcholine bilayers, which give access to lipid structure and dynamics on both sides of the transition temperature. Unlike cholesterol, which is known to induce a continuous liquid ordered phase by having opposite effects on the two phases, we find that membrane proteins decrease lipid order at all temperatures studied. The disordering is stronger at low temperatures, so that once the proteins cover roughly half of the membrane area the low- and high-temperature phases become alike and the transition is lost. Our results suggest that in addition to local cholesterol concentration, local protein concentration may also help dictate membrane fluidity and especially its response to temperature change.

items.title_en: Distinct activation mechanisms underlie ligand efficacy at a GPCR
items.abstract_en: Ligands that bind to the same G protein-coupled receptor (GPCR) can produce widely different levels of signaling. These differences in efficacy are central to pharmacology, yet how a receptor sequence determines signaling level remains incompletely understood. Here we develop a deep mutational pharmacology approach to measure how each residue in the -opioid receptor (OR) shapes responses to 15 opioids, yielding ~400,000 measurements of variant effects on signaling and expression, including full concentration-response series for three agonists. Mutational effects on potency are strongest near the orthosteric pocket, whereas effects on efficacy extend through the transmembrane core and intracellular face. Ligands share many functional determinants, but sensitivity to mutation differs with efficacy. As efficacy decreases, the residues required for signaling shift from the binding pocket towards the intracellular face; partial agonists therefore depend on residues that are dispensable for full agonists. Mutations can broadly increase receptor responses, allowing antagonists such as naloxone to produce signaling comparable to a full agonist and increasing the efficacy of partial agonist ligands. Combined mutations can also reorder the relative efficacies of ligands, showing that sequence changes reshape pharmacological differences rather than simply increasing or decreasing all responses together. These findings support a model in which ligands of different efficacy activate the receptor through distinct allosteric mechanisms which are determined by residues distributed across the receptor. Mapping these contributions across diverse ligands with deep mutational pharmacology provides a way to understand how one receptor converts molecular recognition into a range of signaling outputs.

items.title_en: Unique Amygdala Signatures and Shared Prefrontal Deficits in Autism: Mapping Social Heterogeneity via Naturalistic functional MRI
items.abstract_en: Naturalistic fMRI provides an ecologically valid window into social brain function, yet binary diagnostic labels may obscure neural signatures linked to the continuous spectrum of social deficits. We investigated whether social brain alterations in autism spectrum disorder (ASD) follow a categorical, dimensional, or "dual-track" architecture. We analyzed movie-watching fMRI data from the Healthy Brain Network cohort (ages 5-22) during two films: The Present (n = 327) and Despicable Me (n = 242), using principal component analysis (PCA) to quantify primary (PC1) and secondary (PC2) synchronization and variance partitioning to separate the contributions of categorical diagnosis from continuous symptom severity (Social Responsiveness Scale-2, SRS-2). During The Present, higher SRS-2 scores were associated with widespread reduction in synchronization. In social-motivational hubs (medial prefrontal cortex, caudate), reductions were carried by variance shared between diagnosis and SRS-2 scores, leaving the categorical and dimensional accounts empirically indistinguishable. The left amygdala was the only region with a unique dimensional association independent of diagnosis. Secondary response patterns (PC2) showed further unique dimensional associations in the precuneus, temporoparietal junction, and posterior superior temporal sulcus. No significant associations were detected during Despicable Me; a direct within-participant comparison (n = 198) localized reliable stimulus differences to the medial prefrontal and posterior cingulate cortex, with no difference in the amygdala. These findings identify dimension-specific signatures in the amygdala and in mentalizing-network timing, and indicate that the choice of stimulus affects whether such associations are detectable.

items.title_en: Piezophilic activity dominates the Puerto Rico Trench deep subseafloor biosphere
items.abstract_en: Hydrostatic pressure defines the deep ocean, yet its role in structuring microbial activity across the subseafloor biosphere remains poorly understood. Here, we assessed pressure effects on anabolic activity in sediment communities across margin-proximal, bathyal, abyssal, and hadal settings of the Puerto Rico Trench (493-8,385 m water depth). Community-level responses to pressure reversed with burial, revealing an unrecognized shift toward piezophily in communities down to 20 meters below seafloor (mbsf). Atmospheric pressure yielded higher proportions of active cells in surficial sediments, whereas in situ pressure yielded higher proportions in the subseafloor. Pressure also structured active-community composition; in trench-axis sediments down to 8.35 mbsf, JS1/Atribacterota populations within widespread hadal lineages exhibited a physiological response to in situ pressure, indicative of subseafloor piezophily. These findings suggest that hydrostatic pressure acts as an ecological filter after burial, favoring piezophilic traits that may support microbial persistence in the deep subseafloor biosphere.

items.title_en: Modelling Plant Cortical Microtubules: Curvature Sensing from Bending Energy
items.abstract_en: Within plant cells, the self-organization of cortical microtubules (MTs) into ordered arrays is an important process for directional growth. There is growing evidence that cortical MTs respond to cell shape and/or mechanical stresses in the cell wall, requiring in silico models on complicated surfaces to provide a complete understanding. Most models assume that MTs are directionally persistent, following geodesics of the surface. This ignores the expected tendency of these elastic filaments to minimize curvature. Our recent model incorporated minimization of MT curvature in cylindrical cells and found curvature to be significant in biasing the array organization. Here, we generalize to a larger class of surfaces, studying individual microtubule shapes to provide insights into the role of geometric cues and highlight differences with previous models that use the geodesic assumption. We first show that geodesic models, including current models with finite persistence lengths, exhibit an invariance across certain geometries, leading to biophysically counterintuitive results. Incorporating curvature minimization, we show the difficulties imposed by high-curvature cell edges, elucidating potential new roles of proteins in helping microtubules traverse edges. Lastly, we show that geometries with competing curvature cues result in diverse curves previously not considered. These results provide geometric intuition for how various cell geometries affect individual cortical microtubules, helping us to better understand the processes required for the establishment of microtubule arrays in broad contexts such as: bundles spanning adjacent cell faces in prism-like root and leaf epidermis cells, protruding geometries of trichome cells, and rounded surfaces such as confined protoplasts.

items.title_en: Chromosome-level genome and caste transcriptomes for Africa's most widespread social wasp (Belonogaster juncea) reveal unexpected genomic diversity
items.abstract_en: Belonogaster is an African genus of primitively eusocial wasps. They are widespread and conspicuous across sub-Saharan Africa and yet are among the least studied groups of social wasps. Here, we present the first high-quality, chromosome-level genome assembly for a representative of this genus, Belonogaster juncea, complemented by an RNA-seq analysis of brain transcription among individuals representing reproductive and non-reproductive castes. The assembled genome spans 315.8 Mb with a scaffold N50 of 7.91 Mb. The annotation contained 15,159 protein-coding genes and 20,046 isoforms, with Benchmarking Universal Single-Copy Orthologs (BUSCO) completeness of 98.0% for the genome and 97.8% for the annotation. Using this new assembly, we show that the B. juncea genome differs notably from other social wasp genomes: a single satellite repeat makes up a fifth of its chromosome-scale sequence, it has the highest putative chromosome number in a sequenced wasp genome to date, and it shows high levels of syntenic breaks. We find caste neuro-transcription differences between queens and workers, revealing 573 differentially expressed genes (341 worker biased, 232 queen biased), with significant overlap in caste-specific genes when compared to Polistes dominula and Liostenogaster flavolineata. This genomic resource provides a foundation for understanding the molecular mechanisms underlying primitive eusociality and social evolution in wasps, and opens up new research opportunities for a genus of little-studied insects from the Global South.

items.title_en: Mapping the sequence preference of the generalist class II lanthipeptide synthetase ProcM by mRNA display
items.abstract_en: The biosynthetic machineries of ribosomally synthesized and post-translationally modified peptides (RiPPs) are often substrate tolerant. A remarkable example is the class II lanthipeptide synthetase ProcM, which naturally functions as a generalist enzyme that has not evolved to use a specific substrate during its evolutionary history. Although ProcM has been studied extensively, the sequence features associated with productive modification remain underexplored. In this study, we use the ultrahigh-throughput mRNA display technique to map the sequence compatibility of ProcM across a focused library. This approach expands the landscape of ProcM reactivity beyond native substrates and individually characterized variants. Machine learning (ML) analysis revealed that the dataset contains sequence patterns associated with ProcM reactivity, with models achieving a balanced accuracy of 0.73. This moderate predictive performance contrasts with the near-perfect accuracy reported for specialized enzymes. This suggests that predicting substrate compatibility for generalist enzymes is more challenging due to uneven representation of reactive and nonreactive sequences and limitations of the available data.. Our results provide a high-throughput view of ProcM reactivity and highlight differences with previous high-throughput studies on substrate selectivity of RiPP modification enzymes. Future studies will need to assess whether these differences are common when comparing generalist with specialist enzymes.

items.title_en: Generative steering to adapt proteins beyond native biological contexts
items.abstract_en: Proteins evolved for native biological contexts often fail when deployed in new cellular environments or therapeutic settings. We present ProVADA, a test-time framework that steers a pretrained protein generator toward externally defined properties while preserving functional constraints. Its Mixture-Adaptation Directed Annealing sampler combines coordinated mutations, population selection, and annealing to navigate rugged objective landscapes. Experimentally, ProVADA converted secreted human renin into an active, drug-inhibitable cytosolic protease and extensively deimmunized two murine single-chain antibody fragments to reduce HLA visibility while retaining antigen recognition. ESCAPE-seq measurements confirmed substantial depletion of HLA-I binder peptides across alleles. Deimmunized FMC63 variants retained CAR-T-cell killing and showed fewer binders than a tested humanized comparator. Together, these results demonstrate that broad sequence redesign can adapt functional proteins to non-native biological contexts.

items.title_en: Generative modeling of spatially resolved perturbation responses with CONCERT
items.abstract_en: Spatial perturbation transcriptomics measures gene expression responses to genetic or chemical perturbations in intact tissue. Each response depends on the intrinsic state of a cell and on its niche, the neighboring cells through which perturbation effects propagate. Here we present CONCERT a niche-aware Gaussian process variational autoencoder that embeds each perturbation with the niche of the receiving cell and learns a spatial kernel for each perturbation, whose lengthscale sets how far the effect extends in tissue. We evaluate CONCERT in within-niche prediction, for held-out cells in the niche where a perturbation was measured, and in cross-slide prediction, for a slide from which the perturbation was withheld during training. On a SPAC-seq screen of hundreds of knockouts at single-cell resolution and on Perturb-map lung tumors at spot resolution, CONCERT predicts response magnitude and gene ranking more accurately than counterfactual models trained on dissociated cells, spatial perturbation models and spatial nearest neighbor aggregation. In dextran sodium sulfate colitis, where each mouse is sampled once, CONCERT reconstructs spatial gene expression at unmeasured time points, enabling longitudinal comparison that separates changes over time from differences between mice. The predictions recover the nonmonotonic course of injury, which peaks at day 9 and resolves by day 21. In ischemic stroke, CONCERT predicts responses to lesions of different sizes and locations, in single sections and across serial sections in three dimensions, and reproduces the expression patterns of the lesion core and perilesional tissue. Across lung tumor, colon and brain tissue, CONCERT predicts niche-aware counterfactual responses at locations where a perturbation was not measured and reconstructs missing spatial data.

items.title_en: Rigidity-Aware Geometric Pretraining for Protein Design and Conformational Ensembles
items.title_zh: 面向蛋白质设计与构象系综的刚性感知几何预训练
items.abstract_en: Generative models have recently advanced de novo protein design by learning the statistical regularities of natural structures. However, current approaches face three key limitations: (1) Existing methods cannot jointly learn protein geometry and design tasks, where pretraining can be a solution; (2) Current pretraining methods mostly rely on local, non-rigid atomic representations for property prediction downstream tasks, limiting global geometric understanding for protein generation tasks; and (3) Existing approaches have yet to effectively model the rich dynamic and conformational information of protein structures. To overcome these issues, we introduce RigidSSL (Rigidity-Aware Self-Supervised Learning}, a geometric pretraining framework that front-loads geometry learning prior to generative finetuning. Phase I (RigidSSL-Perturb) learns geometric priors from 432K structures from the AlphaFold Protein Structure Database with simulated perturbations. Phase II (RigidSSL-MD) refines these representations on 1.3K molecular dynamics trajectories to capture physically realistic transitions. Underpinning both phases is a bi-directional, rigidity-aware flow matching objective that jointly optimizes translational and rotational dynamics to maximize mutual information between conformations. Empirically, RigidSSL variants improve designability by up to 43% while enhancing novelty and diversity in unconditional generation. Furthermore, RigidSSL-Perturb improves the success rate by 5.8% in zero-shot motif scaffolding and RigidSSL-MD captures more biophysically realistic conformational ensembles in G protein-coupled receptor modeling. The code is available at: https://github.com/ZhanghanNi/RigidSSL.git.
items.abstract_zh: 生成模型通过学习天然结构的统计规律推动了从头蛋白质设计，但现有方法存在三点局限：（1）难以联合学习蛋白质几何与设计任务；（2）预训练多依赖局部、非刚性的原子表示，限制了对生成任务至关重要的全局几何理解；（3）尚未有效建模蛋白质结构的动态与构象信息。为此作者提出 RigidSSL（刚性感知自监督学习）几何预训练框架，在生成式微调之前先进行几何学习。第一阶段 RigidSSL-Perturb 从 AlphaFold 蛋白结构数据库中 43.2 万个结构出发，通过模拟扰动学习几何先验；第二阶段 RigidSSL-MD 在约 1300 条分子动力学轨迹上精修表示，以捕捉物理上真实的构象转变。两阶段均建立在双向、刚性感知的流匹配目标之上，联合优化平移与旋转动力学，最大化构象间互信息。实验显示，RigidSSL 变体将可设计性最高提升 43%，并增强无条件生成的新颖性与多样性；RigidSSL-Perturb 在零样本 motif scaffolding 中成功率提升 5.8%，RigidSSL-MD 在 G 蛋白偶联受体建模中捕捉到更符合生物物理的构象系综。
items.highlight_zh: 刚性感知几何预训练让蛋白可设计性最高提升 43%
items.digest_zh:
【研究问题】用生成模型“凭空设计”蛋白质近年进展迅速，但现有模型有三个短板：几何结构学习与设计任务彼此割裂；预训练多用局部、非刚性的原子表示，缺乏全局几何感；并且几乎不考虑蛋白质会运动、存在多种构象这一事实。
【方法】作者提出 RigidSSL，一个“先学几何、再做生成”的两阶段自监督预训练框架。第一阶段 RigidSSL-Perturb 使用 AlphaFold 蛋白结构数据库中约 43.2 万个结构，人为施加扰动让模型学会区分合理与不合理几何；第二阶段 RigidSSL-MD 在约 1.3 千条分子动力学轨迹上继续训练，使表示能反映真实的构象转变。两阶段共享一个双向、刚性感知的流匹配目标，同时优化平移与旋转运动，并最大化不同构象之间的互信息。
【结果】在多个评测中，RigidSSL 变体把生成蛋白的可设计性最高提升 43%，同时提高新颖性与多样性；只做第一阶段的版本在零样本 motif scaffolding 任务上成功率提高 5.8%；做两阶段的版本在 GPCR（G 蛋白偶联受体）建模中给出的构象系综更符合生物物理实际。
【意义】这项工作把“预训练几何先验”的思路正式引入蛋白质生成，并强调蛋白质不是僵硬骨架，而是柔性、可动的对象。对药物设计而言，能同时生成合理结构与可信构象集合的模型，比只会画一张静态结构图的模型更接近真实需求。

items.title_en: Kawasemi-Colours: an open end-to-end platform for structure-colour design based on avian structural colour
items.title_zh: Kawasemi-Colours：基于鸟类结构色的结构—颜色设计开源端到端平台
items.abstract_en: Structural colour provides durable, pigment-free colouration by controlling the interaction of light with nanostructured materials rather than by using wavelength-selective pigments. In birds, non-iridescent blue and green plumage arises from coherent scattering by quasi-ordered keratin-air nanostructures, making these natural systems attractive models for sustainable colour engineering. Despite decades of research on their optical mechanisms, open end-to-end implementations that connect biological nanostructures with colour prediction, inverse design and physics-based evaluation remain limited. Here I present Kawasemi Colours, an open end-to-end platform for structure-colour design based on avian structural colour. From published electron micrographs, I assembled a provenance-tracked dataset of spongy, channel and quasi-ordered sphere nanostructures with associated colour metadata. I extracted interpretable structural descriptors, developed compact forward models that predict colour from nanostructure images, and implemented an analytic inverse design tool that generates candidate structures for a target colour. Both directions are provided through self-contained interactive web applications. Kawasemi Colours provides an open framework for studying and designing structural colour from biological nanostructures. By integrating curated data, interpretable machine learning, wave optics, and interactive design tools, the platform lowers the barrier to comparative structural-colour research and provides a cumulative foundation for testing and refining structure-colour relationships as new biological data become available.
items.abstract_zh: 结构色通过让光与纳米结构材料相互作用，而非依靠选择性吸收色素的颜料，实现持久且无色素着色。在鸟类中，非虹彩的蓝色与绿色羽色源于准有序角蛋白—空气纳米结构的相干散射，使这些天然体系成为可持续色彩工程的理想模型。尽管其光学机制已被研究数十年，能把生物纳米结构与颜色预测、逆向设计和基于物理的评估连接起来的开放端到端实现仍很有限。本文提出 Kawasemi Colours——一个基于鸟类结构色的结构—颜色设计开源端到端平台。作者从已发表的电子显微图像出发，构建了带来源追踪的海绵状、通道状与准有序球状纳米结构数据集及其颜色元数据，提取可解释的结构描述符，开发出由纳米结构图像预测颜色的紧凑正向模型，并实现可为目标颜色生成候选结构的解析逆向设计工具；两个方向均以自包含的交互式网页应用提供。该平台降低了比较性结构色研究的门槛，并随新生物数据的加入为检验和修正结构—颜色关系提供可累积的基础。
items.highlight_zh: 开源端到端平台打通生物纳米结构与结构色设计
items.digest_zh:
【研究问题】鸟类的蓝绿色羽毛不靠色素，而靠羽毛内部微小的角蛋白—空气纳米结构让光发生相干散射，因此颜色持久、不易褪色。这类“结构色”被视作可持续着色技术的理想模板，但过去研究多聚焦光学机理，缺少把生物纳米结构、颜色预测、逆向设计（给定目标颜色反推结构）和物理评估串起来的开放工具。
【方法】作者构建了 Kawasemi Colours 平台：首先从已发表的电子显微图像中整理出三类纳米结构（海绵状、通道状、准有序球状）数据集，并保留数据来源追踪与颜色元数据；随后提取可解释的结构描述符；再训练紧凑的正向模型，实现从纳米结构图像直接预测颜色；同时实现解析的逆向设计工具，为目标颜色生成候选结构。正向预测与逆向设计都以自包含的交互式网页应用呈现，使用者无需搭建环境即可上手。
【结果】论文以平台构建为主，强调其数据可溯源、模型可解释、工具可交互；平台将波动光学原理与机器学习、数据整理整合在统一框架中。
【意义】其价值在于“降低门槛 + 可累积”：研究者可以方便地比较不同生物纳米结构与颜色的对应关系，并随着新的显微数据加入不断检验、修正这些关系。对希望从自然界学习可持续着色方案的材料与光学研究者而言，这类开放基础设施比单篇机理研究更具长期价值。需注意本文由单一作者完成，更接近工具/平台型工作，其结论依赖于所汇编的公开图像数据范围。

items.title_en: Solving Paleobotany's 200-year problem with fluorescence and artificial intelligence
items.title_zh: 用荧光与人工智能破解古植物学200年难题
items.abstract_en: Paleobotany has a 200-year problem: leaf fossils are often too poorly preserved to make proper taxonomic identification. Though they are the most abundant, and well-studied macroscopic fossil plant organ, many fossil leaves-- including specimens held in museum and university collections-- appear to lack the detailed features needed to take crucial next steps, like placement into phylogenetic context, generation of ecological interpretations, or reconstruction of paleoclimate. However, we have discovered that under UV and laser light [~]50% of leaves across a diverse survey of fossil deposits fluoresce in a way that reveals spectacularly detailed leaf venation and gross morphology that is invisible under white light. These 'Fossil Ciphers' bring new life into each step of the paleobotanical method, unlocking previously unattainable taxonomic classifications, quantitative morphometrics, and promising new avenues for the incorporation of AI into fossil leaf analyses. With the aid of fluorescence techniques, we can help solve paleobotany's 200-year problem.
items.abstract_zh: 古植物学面临一个延续两百年的难题：叶片化石往往保存太差，难以做出可靠的分类学鉴定。叶片虽是最丰富、研究最充分的宏观植物化石器官，但许多标本（包括博物馆和高校馆藏）似乎缺乏关键细节，无法用于系统发育定位、古生态解释或古气候重建。本研究发现，在紫外光和激光照射下，跨多个化石产地的调查中约50%的叶片会发出荧光，显现出白光下不可见的、细节极其精美的叶脉与整体形态。这些"化石密码"为古植物学方法的每一步注入新活力，带来以往无法获得的分类鉴定、定量形态测量，并为将人工智能引入化石叶片分析开辟了新途径。借助荧光技术，我们有望解决古植物学两百年的难题。
items.highlight_zh: 紫外/激光荧光让约半数化石叶片显现隐藏叶脉，结合AI可破解鉴定难题。
items.digest_zh:
研究的问题：化石叶片是数量最多、研究最久的宏观植物化石，但很多标本保存质量差，叶脉等分类关键特征模糊不清，导致无法进行系统发育分析、古生态与古气候重建。博物馆里大量"看不出名堂"的标本因此长期闲置。

方法：作者对来自多个化石产地的叶片标本做了一次系统调查，分别用白光、紫外光和激光照射观察，统计其中能发出荧光的比例，并评估荧光影像能揭示多少形态信息；随后讨论如何把这些新获得的清晰图像接入定量形态测量与人工智能分析流程。

结果：约50%的叶片在紫外光和激光下会发出荧光，显现出白光下完全看不见的、非常精细的叶脉网络与整体形态。作者把这类标本称为"化石密码"（Fossil Ciphers）。这些图像让原本无法完成的分类鉴定、形态定量测量成为可能，也为机器学习方法提供了高质量输入数据。

为何重要：它把"标本保存不好"这一长期被视为不可逾越的障碍，转化为一个只需换一种成像方式就能绕开的问题；同时为海量馆藏化石的重新利用、以及AI辅助的古生物图像分析打开了大门，对分类学、古生态学和古气候重建都有直接价值。

items.title_en: High Intensity Focused Ultrasound (HIFU) Thalamotomy as a Safe and Effective Treatment of Essential Tremor (ET) in Older Populations and those with Comorbidities
items.abstract_en: Magnetic Resonance guided High Intensity Focused Ultrasound (MRgHIFU) has been demonstrated to be a safe and effective minimally invasive therapy for essential tremor (ET). However, it is not clear whether older adults ([≥]70 years old) or individuals with comorbidities exhibit similar safety and efficacy. This IRB approved project collected EPIC EMR data on patients that underwent MRgHIFU at Parkview Regional Medical Center from January 2023 to November 2025. 68 patients were assessed for tremor severity using Clinical Rating Scale for Tremor (CRST), quality of life using Quality of life in ET Questionnaire (QUEST), and safety profile via reported post-procedure side effects. CRST and QUEST scores improved up to 1 year from baseline in our patient cohort and efficacies in older ([≥]70 years of age) and younger (<70 years of age) patients up to 3 months post MRgHIFU were not statistically different. Effects of comorbidities on CRST or QUEST scores improvements were all transient or did not affect endpoints. Older patients showed fewer total side effects at 3 months (1.17 (95% CI: 0.47-1.87) vs 0.21 (95% CI: -0.09-0.51), p=0.017) as did patients with pulmonary disease at 1 month (1.9 (95% CI: 1.6-2.2) vs 1.1 (95% CI: 0.9-1.3), p=0.036) while patients with family history of tremor showed more side effects at day 1 (1.5 (95% CI: 0.8-2.2) vs 2.5 (95% CI: 2.1-2.9), p=0.025). Age and comorbidities were not detected to adversely affect safety or efficacy following MRgHIFU in ET patients. Further studies with larger cohorts are needed for validation of findings and assessment for equivalence.

items.title_en: Patient and Surgeon Willingness to Participate in a Randomized Trial of Surgery Versus Observation for Mild Cervical Spondylotic Myelopathy: A Cross-Sectional Survey Study
items.abstract_en: BackgroundCervical spondylotic myelopathy (CSM) is the most common cause of nontraumatic spinal cord dysfunction in adults.
