For mild disease, guidelines recommend shared decision-making between surgery and structured rehabilitation based on clinical equipoise, yet no comparative effectiveness study has reported outcomes in this population. Whether a randomized trial is feasible is unknown. MethodsWe conducted two cross-sectional surveys between December 2025 and July 2026: one of patients with surgeon-confirmed CSM recruited from academic outpatient spine clinics, and one of practicing neurosurgical and orthopedic spine surgeons. Respondents rated willingness to participate in (1) a randomized trial of early surgery versus observation and (2) a prospective observational study in which treatment was patient selected. Responses of likely or very likely were classified as willing. Groups were compared using Fisher exact tests, designs within respondents using exact McNemar tests, and predictors using univariable logistic regression. ResultsFifty-four patients and 52 surgeons completed the surveys. Patients were markedly less willing than surgeons to accept randomization (15 of 54, 27.8% versus 44 of 52, 84.6%; p < 0.001). Both groups accepted the observational design (39 of 54, 72.2% versus 51 of 52, 98.1%; p < 0.001), and 26 of 39 patients unwilling to be randomized were willing to enroll in an observational study (p < 0.001). Willingness to be randomized did not differ across mJOA severity (mild 30.4%, moderate 25.0%, severe 27.3%; p = 0.93). Among patients declining randomization, 85.2% cited a wish to retain control over treatment, whereas fear of surgery was cited by one respondent. Forty-five surgeons (86.5%) considered both surgery and observation reasonable, and preference was divided (46.2% favoring early surgery, 48.1% favoring initial observation). ConclusionsSurgeons report equipoise and high willingness to randomize, but most patients would decline random allocation, citing a wish to retain treatment choice rather than fear or distrust. A prospective observational study appears the more feasible route to comparative evidence in mild CSM. Feasibility assessments restricted to clinicians may substantially overestimate attainable accrual.

items.title_en: Benchmarking Recording-Level Clinical Speech De-identification for Privacy-Preserving Clinical Audio
items.abstract_en: Transcript-based de-identification protects textual records but leaves sensitive health information (SHI) directly audible in source recordings, limiting trustworthy reuse of clinical audio. However, standardized evaluations of recording-level SHI detection remain limited. We established the SREDH-AICUP 2025 benchmark to evaluate recording-level SHI detection systems and characterize the approaches. All 22 qualifying systems combined automatic speech recognition with downstream SHI detection, whereas we additionally evaluated end-to-end detection from audio. Pipeline baselines outperformed the end-to-end baseline in transcription (MER, 0.123 vs 0.155) and SHI detection (macro-F1, 0.507-0.653 vs 0.422). Synthetic Mandarin speech-text augmentation enabled the end-to-end model to detect Mandarin SHI that was not identified without augmentation (macro-F1, 0.171 vs 0). Foundation models showed category-specific differences in SHI recognition, and type-aware adaptive routing improved macro-F1 from 0.656 to 0.697. These findings establish standardized reference performance, characterize current system designs, and demonstrate how language-specific augmentation and category-aware model integration can improve recording-level SHI detection.

items.title_en: BanglaDiaHallu: Hallucinations of large language models and the effect of guideline-grounded retrieval-augmented generation in Bangla diabetes question answering
items.abstract_en: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly consulted for health advice, but they can produce fluent statements that are false or unsupported, known as hallucinations, and this risk is poorly characterised in low-resource languages such as Bangla. We measured hallucinations of locally deployable open-weight LLMs in Bangla diabetes question answering and tested whether retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) grounded in Bangladeshs National Guideline on Diabetes Mellitus reduces them. Forty patient questions spanning six clinical sub-domains were each answered twice, under zero-shot prompting, by Qwen3.5-9B, TigerLLM-9B, Qwen3.6-35B-A3B and Gemma-4-26B-A4B, and by BanglaDiaRAG, which adds hybrid dense (BGE-M3) and sparse (BM25) retrieval from a physician-reviewed Bangla guideline knowledge base to Qwen3.5-9B. Two physicians rated the 400 de-identified responses by consensus for medical accuracy, completeness, safety, readability and reliability on a 0-1 scale, and responses with accuracy below 0.70 were classified as hallucinated. Hallucination rates were 2.5% for Gemma-4-26B-A4B, 3.8% for TigerLLM-9B, 22.5% for Qwen3.6-35B-A3B and 77.5% for Qwen3.5-9B. Guideline grounding lowered the rate of Qwen3.5-9B to 11.3% (difference -66.3 percentage points; 95% CI -76.3 to -55.0) and raised every criterion by 0.24 to 0.38 points (Holm-adjusted p < 0.001). BanglaDiaRAG outscored Qwen3.6-35B-A3B on all five criteria and matched or exceeded TigerLLM-9B, but it remained below Gemma-4-26B-A4B in safety, readability and reliability, and its residual errors were specific, confident and potentially harmful. Guideline grounding can turn a weak general-purpose model into a much safer Bangla diabetes assistant, but the choice of base model mattered as much as retrieval and no configuration was free of hallucination, so clinical oversight remains essential before patient-facing use.

items.title_en: Trends in incidence and antimicrobial resistance for five major causes of bacteraemia in a Canadian metropolitan area, 2006-22: a genomic and antimicrobial use cohort study
items.abstract_en: Background Using a population-based cohort from the Calgary Health Zone (CHZ), Canada, we integrated longitudinal antimicrobial susceptibility and prescribing data with the whole genome sequences of five major pathogens. We aimed to assess how antimicrobial resistance (AMR) responds to prescribing changes and determine which bacterial strains shape these dynamics. Methods We analysed antibiotic prescribing rates, clinical and genomic data from 7,271 Staphylococcus aureus, 1,609 Enterococcus faecalis, 801 Enterococcus faecium, 11,363 Escherichia coli, and 2,319 Klebsiella pneumoniae isolates, associated with bacteraemia episodes in the CHZ between 2006-2022. Genomic clusters (referred to as strains) were identified using StrainGST and assigned to known sequence types (STs) or clonal complexes (CCs). Strain-level incidence, stratified by community-onset (isolates collected [≤]48h after admission) and hospital-onset (>48h after admission), AMR phenotypes, and prescribing rates were modelled using negative-binomial and binomial regression. Temporal trends were quantified using average annual percentage change (AAPC). Findings Between 2010-2022, fluoroquinolone prescribing declined in both community (AAPC=-6.8% [95% CI -8.1, -5.4]; p<0.0001) and hospital settings (AAPC=-5.1% [-6.5, -3.7]; p<0.0001). This was accompanied by a significant reduction in fluoroquinolone resistance among Gram-positive species. Specifically, S aureus bacteraemia resistant to clinically important antibiotics, cloxacillin, ciprofloxacin, erythromycin, and clindamycin, declined from 2006 to 2022, mostly in hospital-onset cases (AAPC=-16.0%, [-19.3%, -12.7%], p<0.0001). In E coli, ceftriaxone and ciprofloxacin resistance were clustered in ST131 and the emerging ST1193; the latter increased steadily, particularly in community-onset cases (AAPC=17.7%, [9.0%, 30.0%], p<0.0001). CTX-M-27-producing E coli ST131 strains increased (AAPC=23.8%, [17.4%, 30.5%], p<0.0001) between 2008-2022, while CTX-M-14-producing E coli ST131 declined (AAPC=-15.9%, [-21.3%, -10.2%], p<0.0001) between 2013-2022. These trends were paralleled by an increase in community cephalosporin prescribing (AAPC=7.3%, [4.2%, 10.5%], p<0.0001) between 2010-2022. For K pneumoniae, hypervirulent ST23 was most common (N=88) with an increasing trend in incidence (AAPC=2.3%, [-4.4%, 9.4%]) between 2006-2019. Conclusions The contrasting resistance trends between Gram-positive and Gram-negative species underscore the complexity of AMR control efforts. Effective strategies will require stewardship efforts targeting multiple drug classes, genomic surveillance for emerging resistant strains, and interventions extending beyond hospital settings. Funding This study was funded by a Large Scale Applied Research Project competition award (2017) from Genome Canada, administered via Genome Alberta. IAL is supported by an Alberta Innovates Translational Health Chair and a UCalgary Research Excellence Chair, with additional support from the Canada Foundation for Innovation (CFI-JELF 34986), the Natural Sciences and Engineering Research Council (DG 04547). Microbial isolates were prepared for analysis at the Alberta Centre for Advanced Diagnostics, which is supported by PrairiesCan (000022734). This work was also supported by federal funds from the US National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases, National Institutes of Health, Department of Health and Human Services, under grant number U19AI110818 to the Broad Institute. JTS is additionally supported by the NIH/NIAID F32AI179151.

items.title_en: Interpreting variants associated with congenital heart disease with a regulatory map of the human fetal heart
items.abstract_en: Congenital heart defects (CHD) arise in part due to inherited genetic variants that alter genes and noncoding regulatory elements in the human genome. These variants are thought to act during fetal development to influence the formation of different heart structures. However, identifying the genes, pathways, and cell types that mediate these effects has been challenging due to the diversity of cell types involved in heart development as well as the superimposed complexities of interpreting noncoding sequences. As such, understanding the molecular functions of both noncoding and coding variants remains paramount to our fundamental understanding of cardiac development and CHD. Here, we created a gene regulation map of the healthy human fetal heart across developmental time and applied it to interpret the functions of variants associated with CHD and quantitative cardiac traits. We collected multiomic data from 734,078 single cells sampled from 41 fetal hearts spanning post-conception weeks (PCW) 6 to 22, enabling the construction of gene regulation maps in 90 cardiac cell types and states, including rare populations of cardiac conduction system (CCS) cell types. We find that many such risk variants, both coding and noncoding, map onto gene regulatory networks in valve cells. In an unbiased analysis of 90 cardiac cell types and states, valvular interstitial cells (VICs) show the strongest enrichments for known CHD genes. Nine CHD genes are linked to common noncoding variants associated with other valve diseases or traits via transcriptional enhancers in VICs. CRISPRi experiments show that multiple CHD genes have cell-autonomous effects in VICs, including regulating the expression of other CHD genes and genes involved in cell migration and developmental patterning. Finally, we characterize a CHD-associated noncoding variant whose activity is specific to discrete structures within the heart, illuminating how such variants can impact specific aspects of heart structure and function. Together, these results suggest that genetic risk for many subtypes of CHD is influenced in part by genetic regulation of valvular cells, expanding our understanding of the cell types responsible for CHD beyond the working cardiomyocyte. This regulatory map of the human fetal heart provides a foundational resource for understanding cardiac development, interpreting genetic variants associated with heart disease, and discovering targets for cell-type specific therapies.

items.title_en: A prospective, comparative cohort analysis of influenza antibody waning in Michigan and Hong Kong during periods of low influenza circulation
items.abstract_en: Background: Reduced influenza transmission during the COVID-19 pandemic prompted concern about waning of population immunity that could lead to subsequent surges in circulation. We compared longitudinal influenza antibody titers in Michigan and Hong Kong, two regions with reduced influenza transmission during the COVID-19 pandemic. Methods: In two prospective cohort studies (HIVE, Michigan; EPI-HK, Hong Kong), we analyzed longitudinal serum samples collected from 2020 through 2023 from participants without influenza infection or vaccination. Sera were tested using hemagglutination inhibition assays (HAI) and microneutralization (MN) against vaccine strains. Two-year fold changes in titers were estimated using multivariable power-law models adjusted for age and baseline titer. Results: We analyzed 173 sera from 57 HIVE participants and 259 sera from 60 EPI-HK participants. Initial HAI geometric mean titers ranged from 12.3-123.4 in HIVE and 6.3-40.9 in EPI-HK. Among those with >1:40 baseline titers in HIVE, fold-change estimates indicated waning for H1N1 strains, including A/Brisbane (0.70 [95% CI: 0.56,0.86]), A/Idaho (0.40 [0.32,0.50]), and A/Michigan (0.43 [0.34,0.52]), while H3N2 and influenza B showed minimal or no waning. In EPI-HK, fold-change estimates demonstrated heterogeneous patterns by strain for H1N1, and waning for selected H3N2 strains, including A/Cambodia (0.44 [0.29,0.65]) and A/Singapore (0.48 [0.33,0.69]). MN results were consistent with HAI findings. Conclusion: Influenza antibody responses during the pandemic showed heterogeneous, strain-specific changes rather than uniform decline. These findings suggest that population immunity was maintained for many strains despite reduced viral circulation, with waning occurring in particular strains and varying by population.

items.title_en: Resistance Training Frequency and Muscle Hypertrophy: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Volume-Equated Trials
items.abstract_en: Weekly training volume is the primary driver of resistance-training hypertrophy, but the independent role of frequency can be isolated only when weekly volume is equated. We quantified the effect of training frequency on hypertrophy across one to three volume-equated sessions per muscle per week. Following PRISMA 2020, five databases were searched to October 2026 for trials of at least six weeks that equated weekly volume between per-muscle frequencies and measured muscle size. One change-score standardized mean difference per trial (Hedges g; negative favoring higher frequency) was pooled with a random-effects model, and certainty was rated with GRADE. Sixteen trials (380 participants) were pooled. The frequency effect was trivial and non-significant (g = -0.02; 95% CI -0.21 to 0.16; I{superscript 2} = 0%; prediction interval -0.23 to 0.18); the interval admits at most a small effect favoring the higher frequency. Contrast-specific estimates were similarly trivial, and no moderator was significant, although the moderator analyses could detect only large effects. Certainty was low to very low. Within this range, the data give no basis for preferring one, two or three sessions at a fixed weekly volume. Most trials measured muscle thickness, which does not track whole-muscle growth reliably.

items.title_en: Comorbidity Exposure-Window Definitions and Multidimensional Disparities in Long COVID Risk: Evidence from a U.S. National Cohort (2020-2024)
items.abstract_en: Long COVID (LC) affects millions of individuals worldwide, particularly those with preexisting comorbidities. However, when assessing comorbidity-related risk factors for LC, it remains unclear whether preexisting comorbidities should be defined prior to SARS-CoV-2 infection or LC diagnosis. This methodological choice may substantially bias estimates of LC risk. In this study, leveraging Electronic Health Records (EHR) from 6,130,413 adults with documented COVID-19 across 49 U.S. states in the National Clinical Cohort Collaborative (N3C) from 2020 to 2024, we evaluated the impact of different comorbidity exposure-window definitions on LC risk estimates. We developed ensemble cross-fitted double/debiased machine learning to adjust for individual- and county- level confounders. We found that defining comorbidities before infection rather than before LC diagnosis yielded 8%-314% higher adjusted attributable risks and 3%-34% higher adjusted relative risks across 16 major comorbidities. Comorbidity-associated risks generally declined from 2020 to 2024, while substantial demographic, socioeconomic, geographic, and multimorbidity-related disparities persisted. Exposure-window specification can be a major source of bias in estimates of LC risk, particularly for comorbidities prone to delayed clinical recognition or underascertainment. More broadly, our results highlight how temporal misclassification of exposures in longitudinal EHR studies can distort risk attribution and population-level inference for risk stratification for LC and prioritization of prevention strategies in clinical medicine and public health, respectively.

items.title_en: Deep LLM layers expose passage-level context in EEG during silent reading
items.title_zh: 深层LLM层揭示默读期间EEG中的段落级上下文
items.abstract_en: In a previous report we showed that a decoder can recover open-vocabulary word-level information from 19-channel EEG recorded during silent reading, by aligning short EEG windows with hidden-state embeddings of the presented word taken from a large language model (LLM). That analysis contrasted two of the model's 33 layers: the context-free input embedding and one mid-depth layer. Here we ask how EEG-decodable structure is distributed over the full depth of the language model. We trained one decoder per layer of Llama-3.1-8B, with and without a causal transformer over the sequence of EEG windows. We distinguish word-level decodability from a context-tracking component. Word-level decodability peaks in early layers and declines steadily towards the last layer. In contrast, the context-tracking component of the retrieval gain rises with depth, both with and without a causal transformer. Unexpectedly, a decoder that sees a single 0.5-s window at a time tracks the text passage too. Two new controls dissect this component. A target-geometry control, a synthetic predictor made of the true target plus noise calibrated to each decoder's word-level accuracy, shows that context tracking is not a by-product of word decoding and target geometry. A control that permutes predictions across runs from either the same or from different sessions shows that most of the observed context-tracking is not caused by an EEG recording session signature. Instead, context tracking mostly follows the text. A single EEG window therefore carries passage-level information that a contextual target can absorb. The results locate word identity in the early layers of the language model, discourse state in the deeper layers, and make the choice of target layer a design dial for EEG language decoders.

items.title_en: Distributional signatures of computation: inferring mechanisms from computation time distributions
items.abstract_en: Computational complexity theory provides a framework for analysing abstract models of computation, whereas computational systems operate as finite physical implementations whose behaviour is shaped by their architecture and physical substrate. In such systems, computational organisation cannot be directly characterised from algorithms or internal representations. Building on the use of reaction time distributions to constrain mechanisms in cognitive science, we introduce an empirical framework for investigating computation in physical systems by inferring computational mechanisms from observable computation time distributions. The framework combines empirical benchmarking, which characterises computational efficiency through the scaling of computation time with problem size, with distributional analysis, which treats computation time distributions as signatures of the stochastic dynamics generated by different computational mechanisms. We demonstrate the framework using a scalable visual search paradigm, comparing human performance with three computational models that employ distinct mechanisms of evidence accumulation. Benchmarking reveals broadly similar scaling behaviour for the models and human observers, whereas distributional analysis distinguishes between these models. We show that computation time distributions provide an empirical level of description linking observable computational behaviour to underlying computational mechanisms. This framework complements computational complexity theory by extending the empirical study of computation from measuring computational performance to characterising computational organisation. It provides an empirical approach for comparing finite computational systems across diverse physical implementations, including biological, classical, neuromorphic, and quantum systems, without requiring access to their internal algorithms or architectures.

items.title_en: EEG Lempel-Ziv Complexity vis-à-vis Autocorrelation Function
items.abstract_en: Measures of signal complexity have become increasingly popular in electroencephalography (EEG), where they are often interpreted as indicators of neural information processing, dynamical richness, or conscious state. In contrast, classical measures of temporal dependence, such as the autocorrelation function (ACF), remain more directly linked to known physiological mechanisms and are easier to interpret. The present work revisits, for the EEG practicioner, the relation between normalized Lempel-Ziv complexity (LZC) and temporal autocorrelation in both synthetic and physiological EEG signals. First, synthetic time series exhibiting a broad range of temporal structure and complexity levels were generated using stochastic processes with varying degrees of temporal dependence. LZC and autocorrelation measures were then computed and compared. Across simulated signals, a robust inverse relationship was observed between normalized LZC and the first autocorrelation coefficient, indicating that signals with stronger temporal correlations exhibit lower complexity estimates. This relationship also holds in resting-state EEG recordings from healthy adult participants across channels and subjects, as well as dynamically during eyes open/close maneuvers. Overall, these results show that the information captured by LZC reflects temporal redundancy already quantified by conventional autocorrelation measures. Because autocorrelation measures relate more directly to established neurophysiological mechanisms, including oscillatory persistence, network synchronization, and temporal integration, these results suggest that interpreting complexity-based EEG findings should explicitly account for their dependence on conventional temporal statistics, which may provide a more transparent framework for mechanistic inferences.

items.title_en: Novel adenoma-immune phenotypes are associated with risk of metachronous polyps and colorectal cancer in a bowel screening cohort
items.abstract_en: Background Current British Society of Gastroenterology (BSG) guidelines misclassify metachronous lesion risk after polypectomy in approximately 40% of patients. Building on evidence that immune exclusion drives progression of adenomas to colorectal cancer, this study examined immune profiles in screen-detected adenomas as a predictive biomarker for metachronous lesion risk. Methods Patients undergoing polypectomy within the Scottish Bowel Screening Programme, with surveillance colonoscopy between 6 months and 6 years were included (n=2642). Chromogenic immunohistochemistry (IHC; n=2466), 6-plex multiplex immunofluorescence (mIF; n=331), and spatially resolved 6000-plex single cell transcriptomics (n=7) were applied to adenoma microarrays. Cell density and location were measured using QuPath. Hierarchical then K-means clustering was used to define immune cell density-based clusters, which were compared to future lesion events using Kaplan-Meier curves and the log rank test. Results After adjustment for age, sex, site, size and dysplasia, adenoma CD3+ T cell density was significantly associated with future colorectal neoplasia (OR 1.44, 95% CI 1.20-1.72, p<0.001). Using mIF three immune cell density clusters were identified; 1) high T cell density, low macrophage density, 2) low T cell density, low macrophage density, and 3) high T cell, macrophage and SMA density, with significant differences in future lesion risk (Cluster 1: 22%, Cluster 2: 41%, Cluster 3: 36%, p=0.032). Bulk RNAseq and spatial transcriptomic analysis revealed significant variation in T cell and macrophage co-location and gene expression profiles between clusters. Conclusion Adenoma immune contexture emerges as a possible determinant of future metachronous lesion risk, offering a novel biomarker to refine surveillance.

items.title_en: Accelerated high-capacity 6 mA transcranial direct current stimulation for major depression
items.abstract_en: Objective: Home-based 2 mA transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS) is FDA-approved for depression, but amplitude has been limited largely by skin tolerance. This study evaluated the safety, tolerability, and feasibility of accelerated high-capacity tDCS (HC-tDCS) at 6 mA. Methods: In this open-label pilot study, 20 patients with major depressive disorder received 20-minute bifrontal 6 mA sessions twice daily for five days using a high-capacity stimulator and hydrogel electrodes. A Safety Review Committee reviewed data from the first three participants before the remaining 17 were enrolled. Results: Retention and adherence were 100% (203 of 203 sessions); 17 of 20 received 6 mA throughout, with amplitude reduced for intolerance in one and limited by an electrode fault in two. There were no serious adverse events. The most common symptoms were fatigue (49% of sessions), burning (46%) and tingling (43%) at the electrode, and difficulty concentrating (40%). Electrode-site erythema occurred in all participants, with no severe reactions. At 1 week, 7 of 20 reported a residual skin change, none painful; at 1 month, spots of residual pigmentation were observed at the electrode site in 2 participants, both Black. In five days, mean PHQ-9 scores decreased from 15.8 to 7.2 (Hedges g=1.62); 50% of participants responded, 45% remitted, and improvement was maintained at 1 month. Anhedonia, mindfulness, and self-reported cognitive function also improved (g=0.76 to 1.23), with gains maintained at 1 month. Conclusions: Accelerated 6 mA HC-tDCS was feasible, well tolerated, and warrants a sham-controlled trial.

items.title_en: Effects of Cannabidiol on Auditory Mismatch Negativity in Autistic Children
items.abstract_en: Pharmacological treatments targeting core autistic features remain limited. In neurotypical adults, cannabidiol (CBD) alters mismatch negativity (MMN), an electrophysiological marker of automatic auditory deviance detection that has been associated with autistic traits. The effects of CBD on MMN, as measured using electroencephalography (EEG), in autistic children remain unknown. This secondary analysis of a pilot randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled crossover trial examined the effects of 12 weeks of oral CBD oil on MMN during a duration-deviant auditory oddball task. We hypothesised that CBD would produce more negative MMN amplitudes and shorter peak latencies relative to placebo. Nineteen autistic children (6-12 years, 8 female) received CBD (dose) and placebo in randomised order, separated by an 8-week washout. Age-adjusted linear mixed-effects models tested Time (baseline, follow-up) x Treatment (CBD, placebo) effects on mean MMN amplitude and peak latency separately at Fz and FCz. Exploratory Spearman correlations examined baseline associations between MMN and Developmental Behaviour Checklist-2 (DBC-2) Social Relating scores. At FCz, latency decreased following CBD but increased following placebo but did not survive FDR correction (p = .029, pFDR = .058) and no other interactions were significant. Higher baseline DBC-2 Social Relating scores were associated with more negative MMN amplitude at FCz (rho = -.58, pFDR = .028) and Fz (rho = -.59, pFDR = .028). These findings provide tentative evidence that CBD may modulate MMN latency in autistic children. Larger trials should clarify CBDs effects on MMN and further examine the association between MMN amplitude and social-relating difficulties.

items.title_en: T-cell dysregulation is implicated in the encephalopathy of prematurity
items.abstract_en: Preterm birth is strongly linked to systemic inflammation and encephalopathy of prematurity, which underlies subsequent cognitive impairment. T-cell immunity contributes to brain-immune crosstalk across the life course but its role in the pathogenesis of encephalopathy of prematurity is unknown. Protein epigenetic scores are DNA methylation (DNAm)-based proxies of circulating proteins. We tested the hypothesis that T-cell dysregulation has a specific role in child neurodevelopment following preterm birth. Multimodal data were collected from 144 preterm infants (median gestational age at birth 29+5 weeks [range 23+3 to 32+6]) recruited to a prospective cohort study: saliva DNAm for protein epigenetic score derivation and brain MRI, both at term-equivalent age, and the Mullen Scales of Early Learning Composite score at 5 years from a subset. We investigated associations of the epigenetic scores for cytotoxic and regulatory T cell-associated molecule (DNAm CRTAM) and C-reactive protein (DNAm CRP; a non-specific marker of inflammation) with MRI metrics of encephalopathy of prematurity: global and regional brain volumes, and general factors of diffusion tensor imaging and neurite orientation dispersion and density imaging metrics averaged across 42 white matter tracts. We tested whether DNAm CRTAM explains more variance than DNAm CRP in MRI metrics of the encephalopathy of prematurity and cognitive scores in childhood. Higher neonatal DNAm CRTAM was associated with lower general factor of fractional anisotropy ({beta} = -0.252, q = 0.011) and higher general factors of radial diffusivity ({beta} = 0.215, q = 0.039), mean diffusivity ({beta} = 0.198, q = 0.047) and orientation dispersion index ({beta} = 0.201, q = 0.048), independent of inflammatory morbidities and other biological covariates after false discovery rate correction. DNAm CRTAM explained more variance than DNAm CRP (maximum incremental R2 = 4.2% vs 1.5%) in diffusion MRI metrics. Higher neonatal DNAm CRTAM was associated with lower cognitive scores at 5 years, independent of DNAm CRP and other covariates ({beta} = -0.332, P = 0.008), and explained more variance in cognitive scores than DNAm CRP (incremental R2 = 9.4% vs 1.2%). An epigenetic proxy of CRTAM in preterm infants is associated with both encephalopathy of prematurity in the neonatal period and lower cognitive performance at 5 years, explaining greater incremental variance than a non-specific marker of inflammation. The data implicate T-cell dysregulation in the pathophysiology of atypical neurodevelopment following preterm birth.

items.title_en: Does the Disease-free Survival Benefit of Adding Belzutifan to Adjuvant Pembrolizumab Persist Beyond the Planned Treatment Period? A Reconstructed Individual Patient Data Analysis of Phase 3 Renal Cell Carcinoma Trials
items.abstract_en: Background and Objective: Adding belzutifan to adjuvant pembrolizumab improved disease-free survival (DFS) in LITESPARK-022, but its durability beyond the 1-year treatment is unknown. Methods: Following a registered plan, we reconstructed individual patient data from published Kaplan-Meier curves of ten phase 3 adjuvant renal cell carcinoma trials. Within each trial, we estimated restricted mean survival time differences ({Delta}RMST), hazard ratios (HRs) before and after planned treatment ended, and DFS differences. Key Findings and Limitations: In LITESPARK-022 (central review), the 24-month {Delta}RMST was 1.34 months (95% confidence interval 0.73-1.95), and the belzutifan arm remained ahead after month 12 ({Delta}RMST increment 0.74 months/yr, 0.32-1.19). The HR was 0.55 (0.43-0.71) before month 12 and 1.16 (0.87-1.54) afterwards (post/pre ratio 2.10); investigator assessment showed similar attenuation. Similar ratios occurred in KEYNOTE-564 at its first interim analysis (2.02), whose benefit persisted, and in SORCE and PROTECT (2.09, 2.59), whose benefit faded. From months 12 to 30 (post hoc), the DFS difference changed by -3.7 percentage points (-8.1 to 0.8) with central review and 0.6 (-4.0 to 5.0) with investigator assessment. Data were reconstructed, and follow-up was short. Conclusions and Clinical Implications: Relative hazard reductions with belzutifan were greater before month 12; durability of the absolute DFS advantage is uncertain and assessment-dependent, so single-HR projections should be avoided.

items.title_en: Multimodal profiling for prediction of primary resistance to anti-PD-(L)1 therapy in advanced non-small-cell lung cancer: the prospective PIONeeR biomarkers study
items.title_zh: 多模态分析用于预测晚期非小细胞肺癌对抗PD-(L)1治疗的原发性耐药：前瞻性PIONeeR生物标志物研究
items.abstract_en: Background Pretreatment prediction of primary resistance to anti-PD-(L)1 therapy in advanced non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) remains an unmet clinical need. Existing biomarkers - including PD-L1 expression and tumour mutational burden (TMB) - are insufficiently discriminatory, and multimodal predictive models targeting primary resistance are still lacking to precisely drive patients treatment strategy. Methods PIONeeR was a prospective, multicentre biomarker study conducted across 17 centres (NCT03493581). Adults with advanced NSCLC initiating standard-of-care first-line platinum-based chemotherapy plus anti-PD-(L)1 therapy, or second-or-later-line anti-PD-(L)1 monotherapy, were enrolled. Pretreatment multimodal profiling spanned six biological layers: clinical, routine medical biology, high-dimensional circulating immune phenotyping, soluble vascular markers, tumour immune contexture with digital pathology analysis of multiplex immunohistochemistry and immunofluorescence, transcriptomics and genomics. The primary endpoint was prediction of primary resistance (PrR). Thirty-six feature-selection methods and ten machine learning models (360 pipelines) were benchmarked within a .632 optimism-correction framework. Results Between March 2018 and January 2023, 439 patients were enrolled (269 first-line, 170 subsequent-line); 435 were evaluable for PrR, which occurred in 39.5%. Individual biomarkers showed broad but modest associations with PrR (maximum AUROC 0.64). In the first-line chemo-immunotherapy setting, the multimodal signature achieved an optimism-corrected AUROC of 0.69 (s.d. 0.06) and a Positive Predictive Value (PPV) of 0.51 (s.d. 0.11) against a primary-resistance prevalence of 30%, outperforming PD-L1 (PPV 0.36, s.d. 0.02) and TMB (PPV 0.35, s.d. 0.03). In the subsequent-line setting it achieved an AUROC of 0.69 (s.d. 0.08) and a PPV of 0.64 (s.d. 0.08), where PD-L1 alone performed at least as well (PPV 0.68). The 18-feature signature included stromal regulatory T-cell infiltration, circulating transitional B cells, and multiple routine laboratory variables, with treatment-setting-dependent contributions. Interpretation Despite comprehensive multimodal pretreatment profiling, primary resistance to anti-PD-(L)1 therapy in advanced NSCLC cannot be captured by isolated biomarkers alone. Complete results are publicly accessible through an interactive dashboard (https://compo.inria.fr/pioneer-dashboard/), a reference resource for future meta-analyses. Multimodal integration improved risk stratification while highlighting the strong contribution of routinely available baseline variables. These findings support the development of clinically pragmatic models to identify patients who should access next-generation immunotherapy strategies aimed at overcoming primary resistance to PD-(L)1 inhibition.

items.title_en: Development, validation and clinical implementation of cellular swab materials for quality assurance of pharmacogenomic point-of-care testing
items.abstract_en: Background: Pharmacogenomic point-of-care testing (PGx POCT) enables genotype-informed prescribing at the bedside, but implementation is limited by the lack of suitable reference materials and standardised external quality assessment (EQA). Methods: Fixed lymphoblastoid cell lines were formulated as swab-based materials at defined cellular inputs for MTRNR1 POCT. Materials were evaluated using Genedrive MTRNR1 assays, quantitative PCR, acceptance quality limit batch release, workflow perturbation testing and stability studies, then deployed in an international EQA programme. Results: Materials were homogeneous, workflow-compatible and reproducible, with 100% correct genotype calls at the lowest intended manufacturing cell load. Seven EQA surveys yielded 253 participant results, with full-mark rates between 87.5 and 100%, and six test failures. Most failures occurred with low cell-input materials near the assay limit of detection. The materials supported genotype concordance, performance monitoring and identification of workflow and sample-related variability. Conclusions: Workflow-compatible cell-based reference materials combined with EQA provide a scalable framework for quality-assured PGx POCT beyond specialist laboratories. International MT-RNR1 PGx POCT EQA programme deployment demonstrated feasibility in decentralised settings. The framework may provide a model for the implementation, verification and ongoing quality assessment of PGx POCT. Further evaluation across platforms, analytes, settings and participant groups is required to establish broader applicability.

items.title_en: Restoring Physical Resilience: Consistent Functional and Sarcopenia Gains Across Two Vivifrail Cohorts
items.abstract_en: Objectives: To evaluate change in physical function and probable sarcopenia following a 36-week community multicomponent exercise programme (Vivifrail model) across two consecutive cycles, and to assess the consistency of this change between cohorts. Study design: Quasi-experimental, single-arm, repeated-measures service evaluation. Ninety-two older adults (2025-2026 cohort; mean age 75.9 years, 88.0% women) completed baseline and post-intervention assessments; an independent 2024-2025 cohort (n = 86) was analysed jointly for replication (n = 178). Main outcome measures: Short Physical Performance Battery (SPPB) score (primary); Timed Up and Go (TUG), handgrip strength, 6-metre walk time and Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE) (secondary); probable sarcopenia (EWGSOP2), SPPB-based frailty category, and a fall-risk indicator computed identically in both cohorts. Results: SPPB improved by a mean of 1.33 points (Cohen's d = 0.96; p < .001), with concordant improvement in all four secondary outcomes (all q < .005). 72.8% reached the substantial minimal clinically important difference. Probable sarcopenia fell from 17.4% to 5.4% (p = .006), and frailty category shifted toward higher functional levels (p < .001). Effect sizes were consistent between cohorts for SPPB, handgrip and 6-metre walk; the Time x Cohort interaction was significant for TUG only. In the pooled sample, elevated fall risk fell from 19.7% to 11.2% (p = .002). Conclusions: A 36-week multicomponent exercise programme was associated with clinically meaningful, reproducible improvement in physical function and a reduction in probable sarcopenia across two independent cohorts. The single-arm design precludes causal inference.

items.title_en: Protocol for the development of a tool (INSPECT-IPD) to identify problematic randomised controlled trials when individual participant data are available
items.abstract_en: Introduction Randomised controlled trials (RCTs) investigate the safety and efficacy of interventions. It has become clear however that some RCTs include fabricated data. The INSPECT-SR tool assesses the trustworthiness of RCTs in systematic reviews of healthcare-related interventions. However, where individual participant data (IPD) can be obtained, a more thorough assessment of trustworthiness is possible. Consequently, INSPECT-SR recommends obtaining IPD to resolve uncertainties, though there is no consensus on appropriate methods for forensic analysis of raw data. Our aim is to evaluate IPD checks to establish which are worthwhile, and how they can be implemented in a new tool, INSPECT-IPD (Investigating Problematic Clinical Trials with Individual Participant Data). Methods and analysis Using international expert consensus and empirical evidence, the INSPECT-IPD tool will be developed using five stages: (1) compiling a list of IPD trustworthiness checks, (2) evaluating the usefulness and ease of interpretation of the checks when applying them to a collection of presumed authentic and fabricated IPD datasets, (3) a Delphi survey to determine which checks are supported by expert consensus, (4) a series of consensus meetings for selection of checks to be included in the draft tool and finally (5) prospective testing of the draft tool in: a) the production of systematic reviews, and b) the journal editorial process for RCT submissions, leading to refinement based on user feedback. Ethics and dissemination The University of Manchester ethics decision tool determined that ethical approval was not required (18 June 2024). This project includes secondary research and surveys of healthcare researchers on topics relating to their work. All results will be published as preprints and open-access articles, and the final tool will be freely available.

items.title_en: Combining Randomized and Observational Data: The Case of Postnatal Prophylaxis Against HIV
items.abstract_en: The efficacy of current antiretroviral interventions for prevention of vertical HIV transmission is both a triumph and a challenge for future efficacy studies of novel agents, including long-acting antiretroviral agents. Given the effectiveness of current antiretroviral interventions, standard randomized controlled trials to assess novel interventions targeted towards further reducing vertical HIV transmission may be infeasible due to required sample sizes. To address this study design challenge, we propose a novel augmented clinical trial design, where a randomized trial with an active comparator is augmented with a concurrent observational cohort to supplement the standard-of-care arm. The proposed design and analysis can overcome sampling biases, and an associated diagnostic can evaluate potential biases from unmeasured covariates. The proposed trial design is illustrated with an example and studied further using a simulation study. In the illustrative example, an augmented trial with a 3:1 allocation ratio in the trial component yielded an unbiased treatment effect estimate, as compared to the trial component alone, and the standard error was reduced substantially. Although the total sample size of the augmented trial was larger than a similarly powered 1:1 standard trial, the sample size of the augmented trial's trial component was half the size of the standard trial and within the range of historically similar trials, thereby providing both feasibility and potential cost advantages. Although limitations with this design remain, many of these limitations can be mitigated by careful study planning and coordination. Augmented trials provide a potentially applicable solution to studying the efficacy of long-acting antiretrovirals for infant postnatal prophylaxis against HIV.

items.title_en: Impact of anemia on length of hospital stay among patients hospitalized for severe malaria in Brazzaville, Republic of the Congo
items.abstract_en: Background: Severe malaria remains a major cause of hospitalization in malaria-endemic sub-Saharan Africa, and anemia is among its most frequent severity criteria. Data on the impact of anemia on hospital length of stay (LOS) among adults with severe malaria remain limited in Central Africa. We assessed the impact of anemia on LOS among adults hospitalized for severe malaria in Brazzaville, Republic of Congo. Methods: We conducted a cross-sectional, descriptive, and analytic study of medical records from adult patients ([≥]18 years) diagnosed with severe malaria (WHO criteria) and admitted to four hospitals in Brazzaville between January 2020 and December 2024. We dichotomized LOS as short (<5 days) or prolonged ([≥]5 days). Multivariable logistic regression, using a backward stepwise procedure, identified factors independently associated with prolonged LOS; isolated hemoglobinuria served as the reference severity category. Results: Among 523 patients hospitalized for severe malaria, 296 met the inclusion criteria. Median age was 25.5 years (IQR 20-40); 51.7% were female, and 82.1% had a low socioeconomic status. Median hemoglobin was 10.55 g/dL, and median LOS was 4 days (IQR 3-5). In multivariable analysis, prolonged LOS was independently associated with delay to consultation (aOR 1.25/day, 95% CI 1.09-1.44), isolated anemia (aOR 7.07, 1.23-40.55), convulsions (aOR 5.86, 1.81-18.97), prostration (aOR 4.42, 1.21-16.2), and impaired consciousness (aOR 4.29, 1.17-15.7). The strongest associations involved combined severity criteria: anemia with prostration (aOR 8.58), anemia with jaundice or hemoglobinuria (aOR 16.21), and impaired consciousness with anemia (aOR 33.31). Conclusions: Anemia is a major, potentially modifiable determinant of prolonged hospitalization in adults with severe malaria, with a markedly amplified effect when combined with neurologic impairment. Early anemia screening, improved access to safe blood transfusion, and reduced delays to care could shorten hospital stays and ease the burden on health systems in this setting.

items.title_en: A prospective case-control study of the gut bacteriome and mycobiome in glioblastoma
items.abstract_en: The gut-brain axis may modulate glioblastoma biology, but human data are scarce and the gut mycobiome remains uncharacterized. In a prospective case-control study, we sequenced bacterial (16S rRNA gene) and fungal (ITS) communities from rectal swabs of 23 patients with newly diagnosed glioblastoma and 23 healthy controls. Fungal diversity was lower in patients than in controls (p < 0.001). Bacterial diversity and overall structure of both communities did not differ. Several short-chain fatty acid producers within the Lachnospiraceae and Ruminococcaceae were nominally reduced in patients, whereas the methanogenic archaeon Methanobrevibacter and Nakaseomyces glabratus were nominally enriched. In an exploratory multivariate Cox analysis, a higher intratumoral proportion of ionized calcium-binding adapter molecule 1-positive myeloid cells was associated with longer survival, independent of age, performance status and extent of resection (hazard ratio 0.82 per percentage point, p = 0.04). We hypothesize that the myeloid compartment links the changes in gut and tumor.

items.title_en: A clinical laboratory test-wide association scan of polygenic scores identifies biomarkers of psychiatric disorders
items.abstract_en: Background: Psychiatric disorders pose a significant public health burden, and their complex genetic architecture underlies multiple biological pathways, contributing to a lack of diagnostic biomarkers. Laboratory-Wide Association Studies (LabWAS) leverage electronic health record laboratory data as intermediary phenotypes to link genetic risk to physiology. Methods: Polygenic Scores (PGS) for 25 health-related, psychiatric, and substance use phenotypes were generated for individuals of African (AFR; N=10,473) and European (EUR, N=35,131) ancestry from the Penn Medicine Biobank. Laboratory data was prepared using the LabWAS pipeline, encompassing 78 laboratory tests and 6 vital signs. Linear regression models tested the association of each lab value with PGS adjusting for sex, age, and ten within-ancestry genetic principal components. Results: Four PGS were significantly associated with at least one laboratory value in AFR individuals and 22 PGS in EUR individuals. In EUR individuals, psychiatric PGS partitioned into three physiological profiles: anxiety, attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder, major depressive disorder, and post-traumatic stress disorder shared a metabolic/inflammatory signature (higher BMI, glucose, and monocytes; lower high density lipoprotein cholesterol and oxygen saturation); anorexia nervosa, obsessive compulsive disorder, and schizophrenia were characterized by lower BMI; and bipolar disorder demonstrated a more circumscribed profile with lower electrolytes and renal makers. Substance use disorder PGS similarly clustered: tobacco use disorder and externalizing showed metabolic/inflammatory profiles; alcohol-related phenotypes showed lower red blood cell indices; and cannabis use disorder had a more circumscribed profile. Conclusions: LabWAS reveals physiologic signatures associated with genetic risk for psychiatric disorders, offering new biological insights into their pathology.

items.title_en: Multimodal Artificial Intelligence for Cause-of-Death Assignment From Verbal Autopsy Records: A National Benchmark Study in South Africa
items.abstract_en: BACKGROUND Timely cause-of-death (COD) information guides health policy, yet many deaths in low- and middle-income countries are not medically certified. In Africa, fewer than 10% of deaths are. Verbal autopsy (VA) yields a structured symptom questionnaire and a free-text narrative. Mortality surveillance increasingly records the narrative alongside the questionnaire, but the algorithms used to produce VA-based statistics were designed for structured responses only, so narratives inform physician COD assignment but do not contribute to algorithmic COD assignment. We evaluated whether supervised models could use both modalities to improve COD assignment. METHODS We analyzed 4,999 VA records for deaths at ages 12 years or older from a national sample of registered deaths in South Africa (RSA), using physician-assigned CODs as the reference standard. We trained unimodal and multimodal pipelines on the labelled records: pretrained language models (PLMs) fine-tuned on narratives alone, machine learning (ML) models on structured responses alone, and the two combined at the data, feature, and decision levels. We also prompted a locally deployed generative large language model (LLM) on the same unimodal and multimodal inputs, without parameter updates. All were compared with InSilicoVA, the operational comparator representing current automated practice. We evaluated individual-level assignment, population-level agreement, calibration, and generalization across provinces in RSA, reporting these metrics rather than ranking pipelines on any one of them. RESULTS Every supervised pipeline improved on InSilicoVA by 8.5-15.9 percentage points in top-1 accuracy and 3.5-7.1 points in cause-specific mortality fraction (CSMF) accuracy. The narrative and structured pipelines performed similarly in aggregate but differed by cause: 63.9% of deaths received identical predictions, 11.6% were correct only from the narrative pipeline, and 13.6% only from the questionnaire pipeline, with the narrative pipeline more accurate for noncommunicable causes and the questionnaire pipeline for communicable causes. Against the unimodal approaches, the decision-fusion pipelines added 4.2-5.4 percentage points in top-1 accuracy, concentrated in the most common causes, whereas feature fusion with cross-modal attention improved the less common causes, adding 6.6 points (95% CI, 1.7-11.5) in balanced accuracy and 5.5 points (95% CI, 0.6-10.3) in macro F1. Feature fusion reached the highest CSMF accuracy (95.7%). Paired differences from the better unimodal representative ranged from -0.2 to +3.4 points, with all intervals including zero. The LLM exceeded InSilicoVA on individual-level metrics and reached the highest balanced accuracy of any pipeline (60.6%), while the supervised pipelines retained higher CSMF accuracy. Supervised pipelines had lower expected calibration error than InSilicoVA. Supervised gains held across all nine held-out provinces, including every top-1 comparison and nearly every macro F1 and CSMF comparison. CONCLUSIONS PLMs using narratives alone substantially improved on current best practice and matched ML pipelines using structured responses, while multiple multimodal strategies produced further gains in individual COD assignment. The zero-shot LLM showed particular strength on rare causes, whereas supervised pipelines better recovered the population cause distribution. These findings support incorporating narratives as a core input to automated VA systems and evaluating representative fusion strategies for the intended output. External validation across settings and age groups will support broader implementation.

items.title_en: Demonstration of Logical Error Suppression in a Surface Code Memory on a Cloud-Accessible IBM Superconducting Processor
items.title_zh: 在云端可访问的IBM超导处理器上演示表面码存储器的逻辑错误抑制
items.abstract_en: Quantum error correction can suppress logical errors exponentially with code distance when physical noise is below threshold. Realizing this on hardware requires tight coordination among quantum gates, mid-circuit measurements, and qubit coherence. Device variation, noise asymmetry, and correlations across space and time complicate the translation of these capabilities into logical error suppression. Here, we study rotated surface-code memory on an IBM Nighthawk r2 processor. Performance varies across tested processor placements, which we attribute to differences in qubit quality. We optimize the code by combining short readout, fused measurement and reset, and an XX echo on data qubits during ancilla readout. Compared with standard readout without reset or echo, the optimized syndrome extraction circuit reduces the median per-round logical error rate by factors of 3.8 in the X basis and 1.4 in the Z basis. In memory experiments of up to 150 rounds, the distance advantage weakens, alongside long-lived correlations that may reflect a persistent error component. Under our optimization recipe, increasing the protected distance from 3 to 6 while holding the other distance fixed reduces the per-round logical error rate from 0.53% to 0.24% in Z memory and from 0.52% to 0.22% in X memory. The corresponding error-suppression factors under maximum-likelihood decoding are 1.68 and 1.85. These results connect circuit compilation and optimization to surface-code memory performance and limitations, and motivate QPU and QEC circuit codesign for fault-tolerant quantum computing primitives on current cloud hardware.
items.abstract_zh: 当物理噪声低于阈值时，量子纠错可随码距增大而指数抑制逻辑错误。要在硬件上实现这一点，需要量子门、线路中测量与比特相干性紧密配合；器件差异、噪声不对称以及空间与时间上的关联都会妨碍这些能力转化为逻辑错误抑制。本文在IBM Nighthawk r2处理器上研究旋转表面码存储器。性能随处理器上的放置位置变化，作者将其归因于比特质量差异。通过结合短读出、测量与重置融合，以及在辅助比特读出期间对数据比特施加XX回波，作者优化了编码：与无重置、无回波的标准读出相比，优化后的校验子提取线路使每轮逻辑错误率中位数在X基下降低3.8倍、Z基下降低1.4倍。在最多150轮的存储实验中，距离优势减弱，同时出现可能反映持续误差成分的长寿命关联。在优化方案下，将受保护距离从3增至6（另一距离固定）时，每轮逻辑错误率在Z存储中由0.53%降至0.24%，X存储中由0.52%降至0.22%；最大似然解码下的错误抑制因子分别为1.68和1.85。这些结果把线路编译与优化同表面码存储性能及其局限联系起来，并推动面向容错量子计算基本单元的QPU与QEC线路协同设计。
items.highlight_zh: 通过读出与回波优化，云端超导芯片上表面码距离增大带来明显逻辑错误抑制。
items.digest_zh:
研究的问题：量子纠错理论上能在噪声低于阈值时随码距增大指数压低逻辑错误，但在真实硬件上做到这一点很难——器件之间的差异、噪声的不对称、误差在时间和空间上的关联，都会让"理论上的抑制"打折扣。作者要在云端可访问的商用超导处理器上，实际检验表面码存储器的表现与瓶颈。

方法：在IBM Nighthawk r2处理器上运行旋转表面码的存储实验。作者先考察同一芯片不同放置位置的性能差异（归因于比特质量），再优化校验子提取线路：采用更短的读出、把测量与重置融合，并在辅助比特读出期间对数据比特施加XX回波。用优化前后的线路对比每轮逻辑错误率，并在最多150轮的存储实验中检验随码距增大是否仍保持优势。

结果：优化后每轮逻辑错误率中位数在X基下降3.8倍、Z基下降1.4倍。把受保护距离从3提升到6时，Z存储每轮错误率由0.53%降到0.24%，X存储由0.52%降到0.22%，最大似然解码下抑制因子约1.68和1.85。但轮数拉长后，距离优势减弱，并出现长寿命关联，提示存在某种持续性误差成分。

为何重要：它说明纠错码的实际性能高度依赖线路编译与硬件细节，而不是只看码距；为在当前云端量子硬件上推进容错基本单元提供了可操作路线，也强调量子处理器与纠错线路需要协同设计。

items.title_en: Task-aligned spectral inductive biases in parameterized quantum circuits
items.title_zh: 参数化量子线路中面向任务对齐的谱归纳偏置
items.abstract_en: Parameterized quantum circuits are widely investigated in quantum machine learning, yet how their architecture can provide task-aligned inductive biases remains poorly understood. We study data reuploading quantum circuits with two distinct inputs: a signal that varies between samples and a fixed, task-defined spectral query that specifies how the signal should be probed. We show that encoding the query can change the circuit's hypothesis class over the signal by modulating how its existing signal frequencies are combined, without introducing new sample-dependent information. This mechanism matches tasks built on nonuniform Fourier transforms, whose evaluation frequencies specify the query and whose sampling positions guide its encoding. We examine this connection in a classification task inspired by synthetic aperture radar, where acquisition geometry determines a query for classifying unfocused spectral patches before image formation. Across small-scale spectral and radar-like tasks, aligned queries improve learning from limited data over parameter-matched circuits with mismatched or absent queries. These results provide a route from known spectral task structure to the design and validation of inductive biases in parameterized quantum circuits.
items.abstract_zh: 参数化量子线路在量子机器学习中被广泛研究，但其架构如何提供与任务对齐的归纳偏置仍理解不足。本文研究具有两类输入的数据重上传量子线路：随样本变化的信号，以及固定、由任务定义的谱查询，后者规定应如何探测该信号。作者表明，编码该查询可在不引入新的样本相关信息的前提下，通过调制已有信号频率的组合方式，改变线路在信号上的假设空间。该机制与基于非均匀傅里叶变换的任务相匹配：其求值频率定义查询，采样位置引导其编码。作者在一个受合成孔径雷达启发的分类任务中考察这一联系，其中采集几何决定用于在成像前对未聚焦谱片进行分类的查询。在小规模谱任务与类雷达任务上，相比参数规模相同但查询不匹配或缺失的线路，对齐的查询能改善有限数据下的学习效果。这些结果为从已知的谱任务结构出发设计和验证参数化量子线路中的归纳偏置提供了路径。
items.highlight_zh: 把任务相关的固定谱查询编码进量子线路，可为有限数据学习注入对齐的归纳偏置。
items.digest_zh:
研究的问题：参数化量子线路是量子机器学习的主力模型，但人们并不清楚线路结构究竟怎样带来"适合任务"的归纳偏置——也就是让模型天生就偏向于正确类型的解。缺少这一理解，量子模型的设计多半靠试错。

方法与思路：作者考察"数据重上传"线路，它有两类输入：一是随样本变化的信号，二是固定的、由任务定义的"谱查询"，用来规定信号该被怎样探测。作者从理论上说明：编码查询并不会增加关于样本的新信息，而是改变线路已有信号频率的组合方式，从而改变线路在信号上的假设空间。这一机制恰好对应非均匀傅里叶变换类任务——求值频率对应查询，采样位置对应编码。

实验验证：作者构造了一个受合成孔径雷达启发的分类任务：在成像之前，根据采集几何确定一个查询，用来对未聚焦的谱片直接分类。在小规模谱任务和类雷达任务上，与参数量相同但查询不匹配、或根本没有查询的线路相比，查询对齐的线路在数据有限时学得更好。

为何重要：它给出了一条从"已知任务具备的谱结构"出发，去设计和验证量子线路归纳偏置的可操作路径；说明量子模型的优势可能不只来自参数或纠缠，也来自把任务先验恰当地编码进线路结构。

items.title_en: Leveraging verifiable structure in quantum circuits to find more efficient compilations with agentic AI
items.title_zh: 利用量子线路中可验证的结构，借助智能体AI找到更高效的编译方案
items.abstract_en: We discuss an effective paradigm of utilizing AI agents to better compile quantum circuits when one can constrain bottleneck subroutines to have some form of classically verifiable structure. For example, when critical subroutines are composed exclusively of reversible classical logic, phasing operations, and measurement based uncomputation, one can efficiently simulate execution for classical inputs. This property facilitates efficient certification of approximate circuit synthesis via a form of fuzz testing, provided suitable assumptions on the input distribution. While this pattern was recently exploited to improve quantum cryptanalysis circuits, here we highlight the flexibility of the broader approach by discussing three important applications. (1) The computation of $1/\sqrt{x}$ that bottlenecks real space simulations of the Coulomb operator such as those important for modeling inertial confinement fusion reactors. (2) The decoding of Reed-Solomon codes which bottlenecks the decoded quantum interferometry algorithm when used to approximately solve the optimal polynomial intersection problem. And (3) the quantum look-up tables and controlled application of Givens rotations that bottleneck the most performant quantum algorithms for simulating chemistry in second quantization. We discuss reference implementations of these algorithms and how they can be constrained and verified in the interest of seeding a Kaggle competition designed to accelerate AI-based research into the optimization of their compilation.
items.abstract_zh: 本文讨论一种有效范式：当瓶颈子程序可以被约束为具有某种经典可验证结构时，利用AI智能体来更好地编译量子线路。例如，当关键子程序仅由可逆经典逻辑、相位操作和基于测量的反计算构成时，便可对经典输入高效模拟其执行。在对输入分布作适当假设的前提下，这一性质可通过一种模糊测试形式，高效地认证近似线路综合的结果。此前的量子密码分析线路工作已利用了该模式，本文则通过三个重要应用展示这一更广泛思路的灵活性：(1) 计算 1/√x，它是库仑算符实空间模拟的瓶颈，例如对惯性约束聚变反应堆建模至关重要；(2) Reed-Solomon 码的解码，它是解码量子干涉算法用于近似求解最优多项式交集问题时的瓶颈；(3) 量子查找表以及受控 Givens 旋转的应用，它们是二次量子化下模拟化学的最优性能量子算法的瓶颈。作者讨论了这些算法的参考实现，以及如何为加速基于AI的编译优化研究而对其加以约束与验证，以期为相关的 Kaggle 竞赛奠定基础。
items.highlight_zh: 把量子线路的瓶颈子程序约束为经典可验证结构，AI智能体即可高效搜索更优编译。
items.digest_zh:
研究的问题：量子线路编译（把高层算法翻译成具体门序列）是量子计算落地的关键瓶颈，而AI智能体虽可用于搜索更优编译方案，却缺少可靠的"对错判断"手段——量子线路的输出一般难以在经典计算机上验证。

核心思路：作者提出，只要把线路中的关键瓶颈子程序约束成具备"经典可验证结构"的形式，验证就变得廉价。典型情形是子程序完全由可逆经典逻辑、相位操作和基于测量的反计算构成——这类线路在给定经典输入时可以高效地经典模拟。于是可以用类似模糊测试的办法，抽样输入、比对结果，从而对近似综合出的线路做出高效认证（需对输入分布作合理假设）。此前该方法已被用于改进量子密码分析线路。

三个应用：作者展示该范式的普适性：(1) 计算 1/√x——库仑算符实空间模拟的瓶颈，关系到惯性约束聚变反应堆建模；(2) Reed-Solomon 码解码——解码量子干涉算法求解近似最优多项式交集问题时的瓶颈；(3) 量子查找表与受控 Givens 旋转——二次量子化化学模拟中最强算法的瓶颈。文中还讨论了这些算法的参考实现，以及如何对其施加约束并验证。

为何重要：它把"AI能否可靠优化量子编译"这一开放问题，转化为一个可自动判分、可大规模众包的问题，作者据此筹划 Kaggle 竞赛以加速相关研究，为AI辅助量子编译提供了可复制的工程范式。

items.title_en: Quality-of-Transmission Estimation in Quantum Networks: Compute, Simulate, or Learn?
items.title_zh: 量子网络中的传输质量估计：计算、仿真还是学习？
items.abstract_en: Future quantum networks will rely on control-plane decisions such as routing, scheduling, entanglement provisioning, purification, and memory allocation. Each decision depends on a timely and reliable estimate of the quality of the entanglement that a candidate path can deliver, with end-to-end fidelity as a central metric. Inspired by the optical-networking experience with quality-of-transmission (QoT) estimation, this article asks when a quantum controller should compute fidelity analytically, simulate it, or learn a surrogate model. The optical analogy is useful but incomplete: optical QoT estimation often predicts a scalar transmission margin, whereas quantum QoT estimation must account for probabilistic entanglement generation, random memory waiting times, decoherence, state consumption, and measurement constraints that can make fidelity a stochastic target. We propose a compute/simulate/learn framework for quantum QoT estimation and illustrate it with a simulation-based proof of concept. Our study shows that analytical composition can be sufficient in simple regimes, that simulation becomes necessary when stochastic memory effects shape the delivered fidelity distribution, and that lightweight learned surrogates can approximate simulator labels at much lower runtime cost for online control. We close with open challenges for deployment, including stochastic targets, sim-to-real transfer, data-generation cost, physics-informed learning, and generalization beyond individual paths to full network topologies.
items.abstract_zh: 未来量子网络的控制面需要做出路由、调度、纠缠供给、提纯与内存分配等决策，每项决策都依赖对候选路径所能提供纠缠质量的及时可靠估计，端到端保真度是核心指标。受光网络中传输质量（QoT）估计经验的启发，本文探讨量子控制器何时应解析计算保真度、何时应仿真、何时应学习代理模型。光学类比有用但不完整：光学 QoT 常预测标量传输裕量，而量子 QoT 必须考虑概率性纠缠生成、随机内存等待时间、退相干、态消耗与测量约束，这些使保真度成为随机目标。我们提出“计算、仿真、学习”框架，并用基于仿真的概念验证加以说明。研究表明：简单情形下解析组合已足够；当随机内存效应塑造保真度分布时仿真变得必要；轻量学习代理能以远低运行时代价逼近仿真标签，适合在线控制。最后我们讨论部署中的开放挑战，包括随机目标、仿真到现实迁移、数据生成成本、物理启发学习，以及从单路径推广到完整网络拓扑。
items.highlight_zh: 提出计算、仿真、学习三分框架，指导量子QoT估计方式选择
items.digest_zh:
研究问题：未来量子网络的控制面要做路由、调度、纠缠供给、内存分配等决策，而这些决策都依赖一个前提——快速、可靠地判断某条候选路径能提供多好的纠缠质量，核心指标是端到端保真度。光网络已有成熟的传输质量（QoT）估计经验，本文追问：量子控制器该在什么时候解析计算保真度、什么时候做仿真、什么时候直接学一个代理模型？

关键难点：光学类比只对了一半。光学 QoT 往往只需预测一个标量裕量，而量子场景要面对纠缠生成的概率性、内存等待时间的随机性、退相干、纠缠态的消耗，以及测量上的限制，结果保真度本身就是一个随机目标，需要刻画分布而非单点值。

方法与验证：作者提出“compute / simulate / learn”三分框架，并给出一个基于仿真的概念验证，比较三种策略在不同情形下的适用性。

主要结果：在简单场景下，对单段链路的解析组合就足以给出可靠估计；一旦随机内存等待等效应明显塑造了交付保真度的分布，仿真就成为必需；而在需要在线快速决策时，轻量化的学习代理模型能以远低于仿真的运行时代价去逼近仿真给出的标签。

为何重要：这为量子网络控制器“该用哪种估计手段”提供了清晰的决策思路，避免一味仿真带来的实时性瓶颈，也避免盲目解析带来的失真。文末还列出落地挑战：随机目标的处理、sim-to-real 迁移、仿真数据的生成成本、物理启发式学习，以及如何从单条路径推广到整个网络拓扑的估计。

items.title_en: Anyonic Neural Network Wavefunctions
items.title_zh: 任意子神经网络波函数
items.abstract_en: The macroscopic behavior of a non-interacting gas of Abelian anyons has remained unsettled for many decades. Prior numerical methods employing exact diagonalization in the continuum and on the plane have been limited to small system sizes, at most $N = 4$ anyons. Using the rapidly developing technology of neural network wavefunctions, we develop variational ansatze appropriate for studying continuum models of the Abelian anyon gas. The neural network architecture, which we call "AnyNet", is capable of exactly enforcing the non-analytic short-distance behavior induced by the anyonic statistics. We demonstrate excellent agreement with exact diagonalization for $N=4$ anyons, obtain accurate results up to $N = 16$ for intermediate statistics, and study up to $N=20$ for almost-fermionic anyons, matching perturbative results within a 0.4% discrepancy. We use this methodology to study anyons in a harmonic trap, and anyonic atoms as a model for anyon binding to impurities. We study the structure of anyonic wavefunctions as the statistics parameter is varied. We focus on the single-particle density, the pair density, the angular momentum, and the scaling of the wavefunction as multiple anyons coalesce. This work opens doors to understanding the macroscopic behavior of anyons, for which rich phases have been predicted theoretically.

items.title_en: Experimental Demonstration of a Balanced Travelling Wave Parametric Amplifier
items.title_zh: 平衡行波参量放大器的实验演示
items.abstract_en: Superconducting travelling-wave parametric amplifiers (TWPAs) provide broadband gain, low added noise, and high dynamic range, making them attractive for applications requiring wide instantaneous bandwidth. This is crucial for amplifying multiplexed narrow band signals spread over a wide frequency range, such as qubit resonator arrays, or amplifying inherently wide band signals, such as in spectrometers or radiometers. In many cases, however, the useful bandwidth of a TWPA is limited by the production of the idler tone at an image frequency. For three-wave-mixing (3WM) TWPAs, for example, an input signal at $f_s$ is indistinguishable from one at $f_p - f_s$, which can produce spectral ambiguity when the input spectrum is broadband or not known in advance. We experimentally demonstrate a balanced architecture that doubles the instantaneous image-rejected bandwidth available to a 3WM TWPA by spatially separating the amplified signal from the output pump and generated idler, which resolves the sideband degeneracy. The architecture consists of two amplifiers connected between a pair of 180$^{\circ}$ hybrid couplers, with the signal and pump injected and output through the sum and difference ports, respectively. Using two kinetic-inductance TWPAs, we demonstrate approximately 20 dB of signal gain across nearly an octave of bandwidth, together with pump rejection below --20 dB and an average image rejection of approximately --15 dB over the operating band. These results establish balanced TWPAs as a practical approach to broadband parametric amplification, enabling improved contamination free bandwidth and eliminating the need for complex filtering.

items.title_en: Transport and thermalization under noncommuting localized constraints
items.title_zh: 非对易局域约束下的输运与热化
items.abstract_en: We investigate the effects of spatially localized conserved quantities on transport and thermalization in quantum and classical many-body systems. We consider several related models: the integrable quantum Volterra model, its nonintegrable classical limit, and two cellular automata derived from the latter. Although localized constraints are often associated with lattice gauge theories, our models do not admit such an interpretation. In systems with discrete degrees of freedom, these constraints induce uniform fragmentation of the Hilbert or configuration space. In the quantum Volterra model, we derive an exact mapping of the dynamics within each Hilbert-space fragment onto a quantum chiral Potts chain. We find that energy transport is ballistic, with identical transport coefficients across all fragments. In the nonintegrable classical limit, energy transport is diffusive, and we similarly find the diffusion constant to be independent of whether or not the constraints are fixed (resolved). Finally, in the cellular automata, we show that, despite leaving transport unaffected, localized constraints lead to a strong breakdown of local ergodicity.

items.title_en: Active Learning for Interatomic Potentials: A Review of Uncertainty-Driven Data Efficiency
items.title_zh: 面向原子间势的主动学习：不确定性驱动数据效率综述
items.abstract_en: Developing a machine learning interatomic potential (MLIP) that is accurate for the specific conditions under which it will be applied, rather than simply for the predefined configurations chosen by the model developer, is a significant challenge in atomistic simulation. Active learning (AL) addresses this challenge by closing the loop between candidate generation, data selection, reference calculation, and model updating. Here, we survey more than seventy studies, with an emphasis on work from 2020 to 2026, to understand how active learning has evolved from a niche, on-the-fly training technique for query-by-committee and Gaussian process force fields into a diverse family of data-efficient strategies. he reviewed examples include on-the-fly molecular dynamics, active data selection for fine-tuning pretrained models, kernel- and representation-based acquisition using frozen pretrained models, and reaction-aware sampling for chemical systems far from equilibrium. We explore the use of active learning in elemental and alloy mechanics, hydrogen and ion diffusion, ferroelectrics and effective Hamiltonians of functional materials, reactive and photochemical dynamics, high-entropy and compositionally disordered materials, as well as generative and autonomous material discovery pipelines. Drawing on a growing body of critical, methodologically self-aware literature, we also show that this achievement carries systematic caveats. Uncertainty estimates are not interchangeable across model architectures and are frequently the least reliable exactly where they matter most. We close by discussing the outlook for standardized, uncertainty-calibrated, and observable-targeted active-learning workflows in the foundation-model era.

items.title_en: Scaling of entanglement with distance between subsystems: detection of phase transitions in the $t'$-$π$-flux model
items.title_zh: 纠缠随子系统间距离的标度：$t'$-$π$ 通量模型中相变的检测
items.abstract_en: The system-size scaling of bipartite entanglement can be used to detect phase transitions. We develop a related approach for strongly correlated electron models where large density matrices or large system size scaling are inaccessible. To this end, we demonstrate that phase transitions of various kinds are signaled by a sharp signature in the first- or second-order logarithmic derivatives of the negativity measuring entanglement between small clusters at varying distances. Crucially, we show how to mitigate the effect of quantum Monte Carlo noise at large distances when computing the negativity. Our focus is on the $t'$-$π$-flux Hubbard model using auxiliary-field quantum Monte Carlo simulations. It has the particular advantage of showing three distinct phase transitions in a single model: semimetal to band insulator, semimetal to antiferromagnetic Mott insulator, and a magnetic order-disorder transition belonging to the Gaussian, Gross-Neveu, and O(3) Wilson-Fisher universality classes, respectively.

items.title_en: Learning the self-energy through equivariant neural networks
items.title_zh: 通过等变神经网络学习自能
items.abstract_en: The electronic self-energy determines the single-particle Green's function and, through it, quasiparticle energies and spectral functions, but computing it from first principles is expensive and it is a difficult machine-learning target: complex-valued, matrix-valued in a local-orbital basis, and dependent on a continuous frequency. We predict the dynamical correlation part of the imaginary-frequency G_0W_0 self-energy matrix of molecules from atomic species and coordinates with an E(3)-equivariant message-passing network, the rotational covariance of the orbital-space matrix being imposed by the architecture itself and the static exchange part taken from the density-functional reference. Frequency enters either as an explicit network input or through frequency-specific output heads, and the predicted matrices are continued to the real axis in a representation in which causality and a non-negative spectral density hold by construction. The frequency-conditioned model reproduces matrix elements to below 1 meV on the imaginary axis for the systems studied here, and that accuracy survives the continuation: for water clusters, including a tetramer absent from the training set, and for chemically diverse molecules from QM9, the reconstructed spectral functions follow the G_0W_0 reference peak by peak and the frontier quasiparticle levels are recovered to a few tens of meV. Learning the self-energy on the imaginary axis is therefore a practical route to real-frequency spectra: once the model is trained, and given the density-functional reference it is built on, a new geometry costs no explicit G_0W_0 calculation.

items.title_en: Recursive Operator Localization and Spectral Gap Descent via the Geometry of Local Spectral Expansion
items.title_zh: 基于局部谱扩张几何的递归算子局域化与谱隙下降
items.abstract_en: We introduce Recursive Operator Localization (ROL), a framework for constructing hierarchies of local energy problems linked by linear maps between Hilbert spaces. To address spectral-gap problems, including those arising in quantum systems, we study a realization of ROL by nested subspaces indexed by a weighted simplicial complex. Using spectral gaps of auxiliary classical random walks on links, we propagate geometric estimates upward and use them to turn local spectral gaps at the bottom of the hierarchy into a spectral-gap bound for the global operator. For weighted scalar-valued functions on facets, the ROL decomposition becomes the law of total variance, recovering classical spectral-gap bounds from local link expansion (Alev and Lau, STOC 2020). Moreover, for positive binary spin distributions, conditional influence describes the overlap of the corresponding subspaces, yielding known heat-bath gap bounds from spectral independence (Anari, Liu, and Oveis Gharan, FOCS 2020). The framework also offers a route toward quantum Gibbs sampling, with applications requiring model-specific geometric estimates and energy comparisons.

items.title_en: Expressivity of IQP Feature-Map Quantum Kernels via Reproducing Kernel Hilbert Spaces
items.title_zh: 基于再生核希尔伯特空间的IQP特征映射量子核表达能力
items.abstract_en: Quantum kernels are among the most promising methods in quantum machine learning, providing a natural way to embed data into high-dimensional Hilbert spaces via quantum circuits and capturing non-linear relationships in data. Their learning behaviour is governed by the function class they represent, which is formally characterized by the structure of the associated Reproducing Kernel Hilbert Space (RKHS). However, a theoretical characterization of this function class, and of how it depends on the choice of feature map and its hyperparameters, is still lacking. In this work, we focus on the Instantaneous Quantum Polynomial (IQP) feature map and derive a Fourier representation of the associated RKHS generators as finite sums of trigonometric functions evaluated on polynomially transformed input variables, with a finite set of accessible frequencies determined by the circuit construction and scaled by the bandwidth hyperparameter. This representation identifies three bandwidth regimes with qualitatively distinct expressive properties from localised, through multimodal, to periodic. Numerical experiments on synthetic datasets with controlled periodic and multimodal structure, across data dimensions and feature-map configurations, reproduce the three regimes in both supervised classification and unsupervised anomaly detection, benchmarked against a classical Gaussian kernel. These results make the relationship between expressivity and data structure explicit for IQP kernels: expressive power translates into a practical benefit only when the accessible frequencies match with the structure of the data, which provides a criterion for selecting the bandwidth when the periodic or multimodal structure of data is known.

items.title_en: Impact of Irrep Truncations on Quantum Simulations of QCD
items.title_zh: 不可约表示截断对QCD量子模拟的影响
items.abstract_en: Quantum simulations of lattice gauge theories with continuous gauge groups require a choice of basis (how states of the gauge theory map to the qubit computational basis) and truncation scheme (which of the infinitely many gauge theory basis states should be omitted in the map to the finite dimensional qubit Hilbert space.) The most common choices are adapted to an electric basis for the gauge theory, where the basis states for each link are associated with irreducible representations of the gauge group. Electric bases and truncations are generally advantageous for preserving gauge symmetries and simulating the strong coupling regime, but their effectiveness in the weak coupling regimes of physical interest are less well understood. In this work, we compute relative probabilities $p(R')/p(R)$ for finding a link in the irreps $R,R'$ in the ground state of SU(3) lattice gauge theory using Euclidean Monte Carlo methods and weak-coupling lattice perturbation theory. The observables that compute these relative probabilities are constructed by introducing seams into an anisotropic lattice, and by a similar construction we are also able to measure relative probabilities of different site singlets (ways that electric flux braids together into a gauge singlet) at each vertex. With these methods we can quantify, for example, the importance of higher electric flux states in the weak coupling ground state. These results directly inform what truncations are needed to accurately capture non-abelian gauge dynamics near the continuum limit.

items.title_en: Delta-sigma noise shaping for low-resolution quantization in Gaussian-modulated continuous-variable quantum key distribution
items.title_zh: 用于高斯调制连续变量量子密钥分发中低分辨率量化的Delta-sigma噪声整形
items.abstract_en: Low-resolution digital-to-analog conversion can simplify continuous-variable quantum key distribution (CVQKD) transmitters, but coarse quantization increases excess noise and can generate data-correlated spectral replicas. We demonstrate digital delta--sigma modulation (DSM) for low-resolution waveform generation in Gaussian-modulated CVQKD. In a 500-MBaud CVQKD system over 20~km of fiber, 3-bit second-order DSM achieves an estimated asymptotic secret key rate of 46.38~Mbps at an oversampling ratio of 12, whereas uniform quantization yields no positive rate. With 4-bit second-order DSM, the rate reaches 50.11~Mbps, approximately 97\% of the 12-bit reference. A noise model combining the DSM noise-transfer function with matched filtering guides the sampling-rate and signal-band design for effective noise suppression. We also identify a phase-conjugate spectral replica arising from third-order intermodulation between the pilot tone and quantum signal, and evaluate its key-rate penalty using a linear-replica security model.
